articleTitle: Preliminary path-loss measurement of on-body wireless body area network at 490 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: As increased requirements for high speed and capacity and congestion of current frequencies, higher frequency is desired in body area wireless communications. Especially, terahertz band gains great attention for researchers for its potential capacity and wide frequency availability. In this paper, a preliminary measurement result of terahertz propagation for wireless body area network is exhibited. An antenna integrated resonance tunneling diode is used as a transmitter and a pyro detector are used as a receiver. Received level of the distance from 2 cm to 28 cm are measured and a simple attenuation model of 490 GHz is derived.

articleTitle: Comparison of measured and theoretically predicted rain attenuation at 32 GHz and 38 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Rain attenuation of terrestrial microwave links is addressed here. Statistics of attenuation from 17 short range links at frequency of 32 GHz and 38 GHz spanning over period of more than two years are shown. Statistics of measured attenuation is compared with theoretically calculated statistics of rain loss. Rainfall data used in theoretical calculations come from a network of rain gauges. It is found that theoretically calculated rain attenuation systematically underestimates measured loss by several dB.

articleTitle: Auxiliary elements selection for planar array sidelobe cancellation based on genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a modified genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the selection of auxiliary elements in large planar array, which aims at finding the optimal jamming cancellation performance. The method is subtly designed and discussed in depth. The comparison between auxiliary elements separation and reuse is also proposed. Numerical results are presented to validate the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Digital beamforming receiver for analog phased array by rotating element phase
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Digital beamforming (DBF) technology provides various advantages over analog phased arrays in various applications. This paper presents a novel DBF receiver for an analog phased array using a digital phase shifter. By rotating the phase of each element signal sequentially using the digital phase shifter, the signal received at each element is shifted to different frequencies. In the proposed receiver, the digital phase shifter plays the role of a frequency converter, realizing the frequency division multiplexing (FDM) of the element signal. The digitalized FDM signal is separated into each element signal using digital signal processing, and finally DBF can be performed. The performance of the proposed receiver was evaluated using computer simulation.

articleTitle: Design of a dual-band wearable planar inverted F antenna based on characteristic mode theory
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a new wearable planar inverted F antenna (PIFA). The antenna is co-designed with the ground plane based on characteristic mode theory. To obtain a wide matching bandwidth around 433 MHz, the ground is operated as the main radiator. The 2.4 GHz operating band is realized by embedding a slot within the PIFA patch. The final design shows an extremely small electrical size, relatively wide bandwidths, and reasonable radiation efficiencies in both bands. An analysis of the effect of bending shows the robust performance of the antenna.

articleTitle: 8×8 single-layer 30-GHz antenna with a combined ridge-groove gap waveguide network
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A single-layer linearly-polarized array architecture in Ka-band is proposed in the context of the so-called Gap Waveguide technology. This low-profile antenna combines the corporate-feeding network and the array elements over a single layer, standing out among solutions proposed so far in this technology. Radiating apertures are conveniently backed by coaxial cavities, fed in turn through a novel corporate feed network formed by both Groove Gap Waveguide and Ridge Gap Waveguide. Such coaxial cavities are naturally integrated within the bed of nails hosting the groove and lead to a low-profile 8 × 8 array. The proposed array architecture may be seamlessly enlarged to any size thanks to the scalability of the gap-based corporate feed network.

articleTitle: Modeling and design tools for small antennas: State-of-the-art and future perspectives
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the Convened Session and subsequent Scientific Workshop of the EuRAAP Working Group on Software at EuCAP 2018. After discussing the context, it introduces the rationales of the Convened Session and the Workshop. Both were conceived and executed in cooperation with the EuRAAP WG on Small Antennas and the EuRAAP WG on Measurements.

articleTitle: AMC-backed dipole array antenna for beamforming less vulnerable to nearby metal planes
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a new array antenna of printed dipoles for beamforming which avoids severely negative influence of nearby metal planes. This is made to be possible by placing a thin artificial magnetic conductor(AMC) beneath each of the printed dipole elements which are excited by a Butler matrix feed-network. The multiple beams of the AMC-backed dipole array and antenna characteristics are investigated in the vicinity of a wide metallic plane. It shows that the beams do not disappear with low vulnerability to the harsh environment.

articleTitle: Dual band frequency selective film design for indoor wireless LAN environment improvement
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a frequency selective film is designed to improve the wireless communication environment by selectively blocking dual bands of 2.4GHz and 5GHz WLAN. The proposed frequency selective film has a fractal structure for unit cell design with polarization and incident angle stability. We printed this design structure on a thin transparent film using a screen printing method that has the advantage of large area and mass production for the inner wall of a building. Free space measurement method was used to confirm the transmission loss performance. In addition, based on the measurement results, we use commercial software based on ray tracing to analyze the wireless communication environment of the building to determine the effect of applying the designed FSS structure to the building. It is confirmed that the applied FSS film structure has a maximum attenuation performance of 29.4dB and 15.94dB in 2.45GHz and 5.00GHz, respectively, for the external signal when applied to the actual building.

articleTitle: A broadband metamaterial based radar absorber
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this article, a single layer broadband metamaterial radar absorber is presented. Under normal incidence, it achieves at least 90% of absorption from 5.6 GHz to 9.1 GHz for both Transverse Electric (TE) and Transverse Magnetic (TM) polarizations. The structure is 12.7 times thinner than the wavelength at the center frequency. In order to understand the absorption mechanism, the three near unity absorption peaks at 8.87, 7.16 and 8.82 GHz have been used to study the electric and magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Recent development on magneto-electric dipole antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The magneto-electric dipole was invented about ten years ago. It is a combination of a planar electric dipole with a quarter-wave patch antenna fed by an L-shaped probe. It can be considered as a co-located electric dipole and magnetic dipole. Due to its complementary behavior, the antenna is not only wide in impedance bandwidth, it is also stable in gain and beamwidth over a wide operating frequency range. More importantly, the antenna is low in cross polarization and back lobes. In this presentation, successful designs for various wireless applications are reviewed, including those by the originator and his peers.

articleTitle: Signal-to-noise ratio enhancement of high frequency ground wave radar based on a metamaterial-based transition structure
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A metamaterial-based transition structure is proposed in this paper for converting the power from a radar antenna installed on a costal sand land to the surface wave supported by the air/sea interface instead of leaky wave into the air or sky. With the proposed structure, the power from the antenna can firstly couple to the spoof surface plasmon polariton (SPP) mode sustained by the metamaterial-based transition structure. After propagating away from the costal line, the SPP guided-wave mode then couples to the conventional surface wave propagating along the air/sea interface by mode-matching technique. Simulated results reveal that the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of HF ground wave radar can thus be enhanced over 8 dB in a wide frequency range by adding the proposed metamaterial-based structure in front of the radar antenna installed on the sand land. The design concept can also be applied to the HF ground wave radar to reduce the sky wave interference due to reflection from the ionosphere.

articleTitle: Dispersion analysis of polar glide symmetry with coaxial rings
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this article, the dispersion properties of a coaxial transmission line with polar glide-symmetric rings are analyzed. This symmetry is obtained by introducing periodic polar rings on either the inner or outer conductor of a coaxial guide. By modifying the relative radii of both rings, we demonstrate that a zero bandgap with non-zero group velocity at the Brillouin zone boundary can be achieved. Such quasi-linear dispersion is analyzed by applying both a circuit-based method and full-wave simulations. A good agreement is achieved between the methods.

articleTitle: Gap waveguide based 1-D steerable beam antenna concept for millimeter-wave 5G application
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: With the demanding system requirements for the fifth generation (5G) wireless communications and the severe spectrum shortage at conventional cellular frequencies, multi-beam and beam scanning antenna systems operating in the millimeter-wave frequency bands have attracted a lot of attention and has initiated lot of research activities. In this work, ridge gap waveguide based 1-D scanning antenna array has been proposed. The basic antenna concept is based on several columns of series fed slot array elements where each column of slot array is integrated with TX/Rx module. The antenna is designed at 60GHz band. The simulated impedance bandwidth of a single column of series fed slots is found to be 13% for −10dB S11 level within the band 58–65GHz. Also, a microstrip to ridge gap waveguide transition has been designed to integrate the TX-RX module with the array. The simulated S11 for the proposed transition is found to be lower than −15dB within the band of interest.

articleTitle: On the antenna for long range low power geographical monitoring IoT network
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: An Internet of Things (IoT) network has been developed and tested in the BaZheXiang area in Sichuan, China. The network will be used to monitor the slopes for the potential landslides. The existing Wi-Fi network required more than five hops before reaching the temporary data centre in the hut which is 8km away from the data centre. However, the new system only requires maximum three hops, the real-time geological information of the slope can be delivered to the data centre at the main water dam.

articleTitle: Novel compact multiband antennas for biomedical applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Novel dual-/tri-band conformal capsule antennas with simple configuration are proposed by modifying the ground of a conventional inverted-F antenna (IFA) and shifting the feeding point. With these modifications, the IFA is miniaturized, and yet it is able to simultaneously cover the MedRadio band (401 MHz - 406 MHz) and ISM bands (902 MHz - 928 MHz and/or 2.4 GHz - 2.5GHz). The operating mechanisms of the modified dual-/tri-band IFAs are discussed in this paper. The resulting configurations remain simple and compact, which is very desirable for capsule type of applications. Furthermore, they can also be used in other applications, such as antennas for mobile terminals and wearables.

articleTitle: Caustics, plane waves and applications to antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This article investigates the formation of caustic by reflection produced by smooth arbitrary surfaces considering a plane wavefront propagating parallel to the optical axis and impinging on the reflecting surface. The calculation involves a surface with cylindrical symmetry and an arbitrary smooth surface in 3 dimensions. The analytic equation is presented for implicit, explicit and parametric form of the surface, and is extended to a wavefront impinging from an arbitrary direction. Some applications to antennas are provided.

articleTitle: Frequency dependency analysis of SHF band directional propagation channel in indoor environment
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In the fifth-generation mobile communication system (5G), the millimeter wave band wireless communication is highly expected that it increases the network capacity drastically. The radio propagation characteristics in the millimeter wave band are thought to be quite different from the microwave band that has been used for the current mobile wireless communication. And it is needed to clarify those differences in a comparative way for investigating the feasibility of millimeter wave communication system in the actual environment. Author's research group has conducted channel measurements in several super high frequency (SHF) bands and investigated the frequency characteristics of the propagation channel to solve the issue. In this paper, we conducted the channel measurements in 3 GHz, 10 GHz and 28 GHz bands in a small room environment. The delay and both the azimuth and the elevation directional characteristics of the channels were investigated by using the virtual cylindrical array. The results showed that not only the reflection from walls but also the reflections from the floor and the ceiling were also significant in the early propagation delay region. The results are expected to be utilized for the system deployment of millimeter wave communication system.

articleTitle: Performance data of a new, large compensated compact range for antenna and payload testing of future spacecrafts
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Large compensated compact ranges are designed for antenna and payload testing of spacecraft antennas and payload units. The Compensated Compact Range concept (CCR) of Airbus is featuring two major advantages for such measurements. First of all the compensating reflector design of the CCR delivers lowest cross-polarization (< −40 dB) for frequencies ≥ 3 GHz and its short effective focal length provides advantageous scanning capability of the test zone. The very low cross-polar contribution of the measurement range is a mandatory aspect for testing antennas utilized for telecommunications satellites due to their stringent cross-polar specifications. The scanning capability is of interest for deployed antennas at the spacecraft and allows measurements without relocation of the complete spacecraft for moving the Antenna under Test (AUT) into the centered test zone. This feature is already highly interesting for antenna testing, but much more for end-to-end testing campaigns where it provides a fully radiated test scenario for up- and downlink without touching the spacecraft at all. In order to achieve large test zones Airbus developed already a few years ago a new, larger type of compensated compact range, the CCR 120/100 with a centered test zone size of 8 m and scanned test zone diameters of at least 5 m for off-axis locations [1],[2]. Within this paper the development results and first acceptance test data of a recently installed, extremely large compensated compact-range test facility will be presented. The design criteria were mainly determined by the stringent requirements for antenna and payload testing of current and future communication satellites.

articleTitle: Single layer PCB broadband circular polarisation millimetre wave massive MIMO array
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A single layer broadband millimetre wave (mm-wave) array with circular polarisation is proposed for the fifth generation (5G) mm-wave communication applications. The antenna element is designed to integrate the matching circuit into a single layer. Hence no additional matching and feeding networks are required which makes the antenna element very easy to synthesise a massive array. The array has a 10 dB return loss bandwidth between 26 GHz and 32 GHz. The polar angle axial ratio is less than 3 within the beamwidth of −60° to 60°. The proposed antenna structure is simple, low cost and robust, which we envisage suitable for the massive multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) applications.

articleTitle: Microwave radar imaging for monitoring dysphagia
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Food bolus obstruction in the esophagus associated with dysphagia is an urgent medical emergency, and is at the risk of serious complications without prompt diagnosis and treatment. Typically, computed tomography or plain X-rays scans can be useful tools for the diagnosis of esophagus food bolus, but those methods have ionizing radiation and are harmful to living tissues. In addition, they are difficult to implement portable devices for real-time monitoring. Recently, microwave imaging is an emerging noninvasive technology that has shown great potentials for medical diagnosis. The dielectric properties of malignant tissues behave significantly in comparison with the properties of normal tissues, and lower frequency microwaves are easily to reach tissues of interest. This study investigated the possibility of using ultra-wideband microwave to monitor food bolus transit through esophagus or throat for people suffered dysphagia.

articleTitle: 5G reconfigurable antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Fifth generation mobile technologies demand independently tunable antennas operating simultaneously at a number of different frequency bands. The design of two, triple band independently tunable antennas printed on a mobile handset size PCB is described for 800, 1500 and 2000 MHz bands. The two antennas are printed at the top and bottom of the PCB offering diversity. The antennas operate independently of each other tuning across the three frequency bands without affecting the resonances of the other bands.

articleTitle: The universal structure of a segment of the microstrip transmission line as a basic element of compact microwave devices
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper a universal structure of the microstrip transmission line segment with stubs that significantly reduce the sizes of passive microwave devices is proposed. Quarter-wave segments of regular lines, which consist of standard designs, are large, especially at low frequencies. The replacement of these elements with the proposed basic element ensured a reduction in the overall dimensions of the devices while maintaining their electrical characteristics. In order to maximize the effectiveness of miniaturization, additional stubs of the proposed structures are placed inside the free space of devices, such as a coupler. Three-dimensional electrodynamic modeling and experimental results confirm the operability of the proposed method. The method considered allowed to reduce the dimensions of the branch-line coupler and the rat-race coupler with respect to the conventional design by 75.7% and 77.5% relational, while maintaining the characteristics of the device in a sufficiently wide frequency band.

articleTitle: A printed wideband array antenna with 45° polarization for 5G applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A wideband 45° polarized element with simple structure has been proposed. With the aid of a corporate feeding network and substrate integrated waveguide, a 4 × 4 array antenna has been designed and fabricated using printed-circuit-board technology. Experiments show that the array covers over 24.4% bandwidth with gains around 20.0 dBi, which validates that it can be used for future 5G applications.

articleTitle: Reflector antenna optimization using one-sided least-squares
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Numerical optimization is commonly used for the design of reflector antennas that produce a contoured beam. The optimization problems that arise in this context are generally nonlinear and difficult to solve to global optimality. Different problem formulations lead to different properties and challenges. We demonstrate that the popular minimax approach can have many local minima and that a local optimization method with a poor initialization may result in a bad design. As an alternative to the minimax approach, we propose a one-sided least-squares formulation. We outline a trust-region method for finding a local minimum, and we illustrate the merits of the new approach with some numerical examples. In particular, our preliminary results indicate that our method is often less sensitive to the initial design than the minimax method. Finally, we investigate the use of the one-sided least-squares model as a means to find an initial guess for the minimax approach, and our results show that it sometimes leads to a better local minimum, and hence improves the design.

articleTitle: Antenna concepts for board-to-board communication
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, the challenges related to board-toboard communication based on on-chip technology in modern high computing environments are evaluated. As a realization for a suitable communication channel, a beam forming network enabling beam switching of a related antenna or array is necessary. For such a beam forming network, the Butler matrix is chosen and explained in more detail, while the benefits of this particular structure are lined out and compared to alternative solutions. A 4 × 4 Butler matrix in benzocyclobutene technology is realized and first results for the performance at an operational frequency of about 180 GHz are given. Regarding the antennas, a half-cloverleaf antenna and a stacked Vivaldi antenna are presented as suitable candidates for integration alongside the Butler matrix and simulated as well as measured radiation characteristics at 180 GHz are shown.

articleTitle: Beam-steering Ka-band phase rotation cells-based transmit-array for circular-polarization
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Planar transmit-arrays (TAs) have been an attractive solution as gain-enhancers for various applications, e.g. satellite communications. For the first time, a TA composed of sequentially rotated cells is employed as beam-steering circular polarization Ka-band satellite ground terminal. Moreover, it is shown that the intrinsic filtering effect of phase rotation (PR) cells for this kind of TA enables improvement in the axial ratio bandwidth. The performance of the TA is evaluated through simulation. The TA presents only 2.7dB loss over zenith scan between 15° and 50° while its structure rotation provides 360° azimuth scan. The TA offers 2GHz (28.7–30.7GHz) combined 3dB axial ratio and 3dB gain bandwidth.

articleTitle: Simple surface-wave launching by parallel-plate and microstrip feeding for leaky-wave antennas and other planar guided-wave applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A simple parallel-plate waveguide (PPW) with a microstrip feed is proposed for efficient TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> surface-wave (SW) mode excitation. In particular, by means of a truncated PPW and a printed sub-wavelength matching section, phase constants can be tailored and matched at discontinuities. This surface-wave launcher (SWL) offers an attractive microstrip feeding approach to LWAs and is an alternative to more conventional feeding networks that are typically employed for dielectric image guides (DIGs) and other planar structures because of its good performance, low cost and simple implementation. The proposed SWL has been designed to operate at K and K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> bands in a substrate with a relative permittivity of 10.2. In order to validate its performance in a LWA or for other planar applications, several scenarios have been designed and simulated: an end-to-end test circuit, a 1-D LWA and a DIG feeder. High efficiency and wideband operation have been obtained for all these structures. The proposed SWL with a microstrip feed can also be useful for other planar wave guiding structures at microwave and millimeter-wave frequencies.

articleTitle: Low-cost transfer printing of antennas for smart textiles
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper we present a grounded patch antenna that was designed and fabricated using a combination of the low-cost high-throughput techniques of screen printing and transfer printing. The advantage of these techniques is they allow the ground plane and antenna plane to be transfer printed in a single step. Conductive thread and conductive connecting snaps were built into the antenna for the purpose of attaching integrated circuits and sensing devices. In the demo case, the antenna is designed to meet the 900MHz band of LoRa networks.

articleTitle: A bespoke lens for a slot log-spiral excitation
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a bespoke lens has been designed for a slot log-spiral excitation. The performance of this lens is compared with a conventional hyper-hemispherical lens. Using the bespoke lens methodology, the specific electromagnetic properties of the slot log-spiral excitation are obtained and its phase fronts are transformed to flat phase fronts by a QCTO (quasi-conformal transformation optics) technique. The performance of the lenses is evaluated with the radiation properties. The bespoke lens produces an improvement in terms of directivity and side lobe levels.

articleTitle: An invisible gradient-index lens with negative refractive index
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A radially inhomogeneous (gradient-index) lens made of material with negative refractive index, invisible from the viewpoint of geometrical optics, is proposed and designed. The geometrical-optics design and analysis include derivation and solution of an equation for determining the refractive index profile, as well as derivation of an expression allowing calculation of the ray trajectories in the lens. The features of the proposed lens revealed in the study are compared to those of the positive-index invisible lens proposed and considered in the previous publications.

articleTitle: MIMO device performance testing with the wireless cable method
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Conducted cable testing has been dominantly utilized in the industry to evaluate multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) capable mobile terminals. However, direct RF cable connection introduces many practical problems. Therefore, radiated testing, where built-in antennas on the mobile terminal is utilized as RF interface to receive desired testing signals, is highly desirable. Wireless cable method is a radiated testing method, where signals can be guided over-the-air to respective antenna ports, just like in the conducted cable case but without RF cable connection. In this paper, several different ways to achieve wireless cable connection for mobile terminal performance testing in the radiated setup is discussed. Validation of the wireless cable method is done both in simulation and active throughput measurements. Future directions and applicability of the wireless cable method are also discussed.

articleTitle: A novel metamaterial element for compressed sensing imaging system
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Based on the metamaterial and the Compressed Sensing(CS) theory, a novel element is designed working for the imaging system. The CELC-JC element is composed of the Complementary Electric-LC and Jerusalem cross element. In view of the works in the metamaterial imaging, the element with Jerusalem cross can increase the efficiency to compensate the loss of dielectric substrate and metal in Ka band or even higher band. Then the object information can be detected by the antenna and the image reconstruction is done in MATLAB to assess the correctness and feasibility of the metamaterial aperture. From the calculation results of the 2D imaging, the rationality of the design is tested and verified and the novel metamaterial aperture can be applied in the millimeter wave and THz imaging for security and detection in the airport and high-speed rail.

articleTitle: Compact broadband inverted-l filtering microstrip antenna with multiple-mode resonator
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a compact broadband inverted-L filtering microstrip antenna is proposed using multiple-mode resonator (MMR). The filter consists of a stub-loaded MMR, and the inverted-L antenna performs not only a radiator but also the last resonator of the bandpass filter (BPF). The two resonant modes can be controlled by the length of the antenna and the length of the open-ended stub, respectively. The filtering microstrip antenna has a wide impedance bandwidth, flat gain frequency response and a designable radiation null can be realized to achieve the sharp skirt.

articleTitle: A radial transmission line model for mantle cloaking with impedance metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this work, the problem of reducing the scattering from conductive cylinders is reformulated by considering a matching problem with radial transmission lines. A unique compact closed-form solution for the surface impedance loads Z<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">s</inf>(m,kb) above a cylindrical grounded dielectric substrate is found without any approximation as a function of the harmonic index m (scattering mode to suppress) and of the frequency regime kb (product of wavenumber k and radius b of the cloaked system). Possible implementations with a microstrip-line based metasurface are discussed and presented.

articleTitle: Antenna measurement based on very near field scanning
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper points out that the measurement based on Very near field scanning is a advisable choice to improve the test speed and reduce the cost of testing for the huge test workload of the future 5G antenna. Several very near field test results can be combined together to form a large synthetic test surface, and larger antennas can be measured. Measurement experiments show that using plastic cart to support the antenna away from the ground, is more accurate than measuring the antenna near ground. The gain measurement accuracy is within 1 dB. 3dB beam width measurement results are generally accurate. Compared with the reference value, the first side lobe suppression parameter measurement results are small, the error can reach 5dB ∼ 10dB. Further research will be carried out using ancillary automatic mechanical devices.

articleTitle: Antenna measurements at millimeter wavelengths — overview
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Testing of electrically large antennas as well as that of electrically small integrated antennas at millimeter wavelengths is very challenging. In this overview we discuss the physical and technical challenges and limitations in testing of the various kinds of mm-wave antennas.

articleTitle: Compact double-frequency microstrip coupler
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The given research work represents a study of a compact construction of microstrip two-line coupler which can work at two selectable frequencies. The featured configuration has much smaller dimensions in comparison with a standard construction. Reduction of dimensions is performed by means of application of low-frequency filters which have the same phase shifts as the microstrip sections replaced. It is worth noting that longitudinal dimensions of such filters are smaller than the ones of a standard microstrip line. We have performed numerical simulation of a coupler device working at two frequencies: 770 MHz and 1950 MHz. The geometrical dimensions of the construction obtained using low-frequency filters are 70.1% smaller than those of a standard construction.

articleTitle: Compact frequency reconfigurable magneto-electric crossed dipole in VHF band
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Reducing the size of wideband antennas operating in the Very High Frequency band from 100 to 400 MHz is a great challenge. At 100 MHz, the wavelength size is 3 m and any size reduction makes the integration easier and reduces fabrication costs. The original technique proposed in this communication enables a significant height reduction (up to 50%) of a Magneto-electric crossed dipole (MECD) antenna while maintaining an ultra-wideband operation bandwidth from 92 to 360 MHz (118%). The proposed technique is based on adding frequency reconfigurable concept on a compact antenna. The profile reduction technique and simulated results are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Conical surface mount short horn for circular polarized patch antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, conical surface mount short horns for circularly polarized patch antennas are presented. The design of the conical short horn for circularly polarized narrowband stubs-integrated microstrip patch antenna and a wideband square slot antenna is discussed. The radiation characteristics such as the return loss, realized gain and axial ratios of the circularly polarized antennas with and without conical surface mount horn are discussed for varying height of the cone. The gain is observed to be improved by around 4 dB while maintaining the axial ratio in both cases of circularly polarized antennas.

articleTitle: Enhancing quantitative microwave holography in tissue imaging
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Quantitative microwave holography is a recently developed direct inversion imaging algorithm. This method shows promise in medical imaging due to its low computational cost and ability to quantitatively estimate the tissue permittivity. However, it faces challenges regarding nonphysical permittivity values (i.e., real relative permittivity less than 1, and imaginary relative permittivity greater than 0) in the reconstructed images. Here, we propose an optimization method capable of removing nonphysical values. This approach is demonstrated in a tissue imaging experiment. Additionally, we discuss the impact of phase wrapping on the Rytov's approximation-based version of quantitative microwave holography.

articleTitle: Accurate and simplified network model for composite right-left handed transmission line
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a general and simplified design method for composite right-left handed transmission line (CRLH-TL) with arbitrary number of unit cells is proposed and validated. In the cases where tens of cascaded cells are required to achieve high radiation efficiency or narrow beamwidth, the optimum design of CRLH-TL is prohibitively computational expensive. Since the optimum design of multi-cell CRLH-TL can't be obtained through single cell optimization directly, due to the existence of inter-cell coupling effect and the end-cell discontinuity. To overcome this disadvantage, we develop an accurate network model for arbitrary length multi-cell CRLH-TL by accounting for the inter-cell coupling effect and the end-cell effect, where only less than 4 cascaded unit cells are needed to extract the inter-cell and end-cell effect. The accurate network model obtained with low cost is then exploited in the CRLH-TL optimization procedure to reduce the computational burden. To validate the proposed method, a CRLH-TL based leaky wave antenna with 30 unit cells is design and optimized. The multi-cell CRLH-TL network model accuracy is verified by comparing the radiation characteristic predicted by the network model with that from CST simulation. The prediction error of the radiation angle and radiation beamwidth is less than 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup>, respectively. Moreover, the time cost of the optimization procedure has been significantly reduced to less than 10%.

articleTitle: Wideband dual-circularly polarised feed for compact antenna test ranges with low cross polarisation
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a wideband dual-circularly polarised feed system centred at the Ka band, based on an easy-to-build waveguide polariser. It covers the band from 30 GHz to 40 GHz showing excellent cross-polar discrimination and an input return loss better than 20 dB along the full band. The system is composed of a turnstile orthomode transducer, the waveguide polariser, and a choked horn.

articleTitle: A gain and bandwidth enhancement for SIW cavity array antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A high gain broadband array antenna is designed using low-cost PCB technology. The antenna consists of two PCB substrate layers and an aluminium plate loaded with cross-slots. The aluminium plate is fixed at the top of the antenna providing a 3.5 dB gain enhancement, as well as better a impedance matching. The simulated results show that the −10 dB impedance bandwidth is wider than 19%(42.3–51.3 GHz) and a flat gain of 20 dBi is obtained at the whole frequency band.

articleTitle: Three-stage self-interference cancellation for small form factor realization of in-band full duplex
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) radio transceivers, which transmit and receive on the same frequency at the same time may potentially double the spectral efficiency of future radio networks. However, to achieve this requires high isolation between the transmitter and receiver in order to suppress the self-interference (SI) which results from the co-located co-channel transmitter and receiver. This paper presents an IBFD transceiver architecture which consists of two stages of RF cancellation and one stage of digital baseband cancellation. A prototype based on this architecture has been implemented and performance measured. The system operates over a 20 MHz bandwidth at 720 MHz, and achieves 100 dB of transmit-to-receive isolation, suppressing the SI to within 3 dB of the noise floor of the receiver.

articleTitle: About the beam cosines and the radiation efficiency of a multiport antenna array
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The paper establishes some properties of the matrix of the beam cosines of the radiated power of a multiport antenna array (MAA), and of the matrix of the beam cosines of the delivered power, which concerns reception by the MAA. These matrices are related to several quantities used in the literature. Though these matrices are usually different and complex, the paper explains why they may be equal and real, under certain assumptions. The paper also proposes a definition and an investigation of the radiation efficiency of the MAA.

articleTitle: Dielectric properties of biological tissues: Achieving accurate data as the basis for novel medical device development
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: An overview of the metrological aspects of accurate and traceable measurements of the complex permittivity of biological tissue in the frequency range 100 kHz to 50 GHz is presented. The topics that are discussed include sample conditioning, coaxial sensor methods (for 30 MHz to 50 GHz), and admittance cell methods (for below 30 MHz).

articleTitle: A cognitive radio simulator for mobile autonomous reconfigurable antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a cognitive radio environment is simulated and used to control the state of a reconfigurable antenna structure in a mobile device's setting. Every active user in the network relies on the state of its corresponding reconfigurable antenna to determine the different modes of operation and the corresponding communication protocols. A reconfigurable antenna design is tested on the cognitive radio simulator by relying on a microcontroller that bridges between the cognitive radio simulator and the reconfigurable antenna. The implemented simulator can control the operation of any reconfiguration technique that is integrated within the antenna structure. As a proof concept, a PIN diode based frequency reconfigurable meandered monopole antenna is demonstrated in this paper to validate the proposed system.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of filamentary sources in the presence of periodically spaced nonreciprocal cylindrical scatterers
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Radiation from a system consisting of a magnetic-current filament and a periodic array of gyrotropic cylindrical scatterers is studied. It is assumed that the filamentary source and the scatterers have infinite length and are located in free space. The far-zone radiation pattern of such a system is calculated in the case where the source frequency is close to the surface plasmon resonance frequencies of the array elements filled with a cold collisionless magnetoplasma. The influence of nonreciprocal properties of the magnetized plasma medium inside the cylinders on the radiation pattern is analyzed with application to the plasma-based arrays operated in the radio-frequency range.

articleTitle: Beam switching collocated antennas for WLAN systems
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this work, we propose new dual polarized antennas with beam switching ability. These types of antennas can find applications in Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) systems with Multiple Inputs Multiple Outputs (MIMO) technologies. Collocated folded monopole and Inverted-F Antenna (IFA) radiators are designed and optimized. Two configurations are analyzed at 2.4GHz and 5GHz bands with broadband and high isolation performance characteristics. By using collocated dual polarized elements with PIN diodes for beam switching, a dual-band dual-polarized 8 port array was designed and fabricated for Wireless Fidelity (WiFi) access point. Experimental results are presented to validate the proposed concept.

articleTitle: Beam-switching antenna using a novel triangular active frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a beam-steering antenna based on a new active triangular frequency selective surface (ATFSS) is presented. This ATFSS operates at 5.8 GHz and surrounded an omnidirectional patch antenna to form a reconfigurable antenna. Two metallic passive frequency selective surfaces with diamond shape are connected to each other using a high-frequency pin-diode to form a novel ATFSS unit cell. This novel ATFSS is used to design a beam-steering antenna covering all azimuth angles. By controlling states of the pin-diode, the reflection and transmission characteristics of the proposed ATFSS unit-cell structure can be controlled, and the gain is also enhanced by a value of about 3.95 dBi. This antenna can effectively operate over a bandwidth of 647.8 MHz.

articleTitle: Further analysis of retrodirective cross-eye jamming: Polarization considerations
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: An analysis of the antenna polarizations on retrodirective cross-eye jamming (RCJ) in a radar system is presented. The effect of the polarization mismatch between the two antennas in a basic retrodirective loop (RL) in RCJ is investigated.

articleTitle: Improved accuracy combined source and magnetic field integral equations with low-order discretization
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A low-order discretization scheme for the magnetic field integral equation (MFIE) with considerably improved accuracy is discussed and analyzed. The formulation is based on the classical form of the MFIE discretized with Rao-Wilton-Glisson functions and introduces weak-form basis transformations, which have recently been employed with great success within the context of the so-called combined source integral equation. Only the identity operator discretization, which is known to be a major error source, is modified in order to obtain highly accurate solutions. Numerical results are given to corroborate the effectiveness of the new scheme.

articleTitle: 3.5-THz quantum-cascade laser emission from dual diagonal feedhorns
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We present antenna-pattern measurements obtained from a double-metal supra-terahertz-frequency (supra-THz) quantum cascade laser (QCL) mounted within a mechanically micro-machined waveguide cavity and dual diagonal feedhorn assembly. With the QCL operating in continuous-wave mode at 3.5 THz, and at an ambient temperature of ∼60 K, emission from both laser facets has been simultaneously directed to a suitable supra-THz detector mounted on a multi-axis linear scanner. Comparison of simulated and measured far-field antenna patterns shows an excellent degree of correlation between beamwidth (full-width-half-maximum) and sidelobe content. Furthermore, when compared with unmounted equivalents, very substantially enhanced QCL beam profiles are observed. Our novel device demonstrates the effectiveness of diagonal feedhorns intended for use in future spaceborne Earth-observing supra-THz heterodyne radiometers.

articleTitle: Spatial mode approaches to enhancing transport communications capacities
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Transport communications systems face challenges relating to the number, density and velocity of passengers. In the rail environment, it would be advantageous to be able to provide broadband-like data connectivity to all passengers. Due to the limited number of connection points into trackside fibre-optic cables (ca. one per 5 km), and the limited spacing possible between trackside-to-train links (ca. 100m due to fog), novel solutions for track-side communications backbones are needed. We estimate the total capacity as being in the order of 40 Gbit/s, which requires the investigation of novel means of providing spectral efficiency. Spatial modes offer significant benefits, but also bring challenges such as requiring large antenna apertures, which may be tackled by using partial aperture antenna approaches or by employing lenses.

articleTitle: Layered patch antenna structure for gain enhancement of 4×4 system
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a 2-layer patch antenna structure based on the combination of polarization and phase difference. The 2-layer structure can control the phase of each horizontal and vertical polarization, therefore, 4 types of signal can be distinguished based on the orthogonality of polarization and phase difference. Some cases of the phase difference have been compared, to find the best combination for the maximum system channel capacity. The correlation coefficient variation among antenna elements has been verified to explain the effect of phase difference to the increase of channel capacity. The system channel capacity is analyzed to show the effectiveness of proposed antenna based MIMO system. Compared with the conventional 4×4 polarization MIMO system, 0°, 90° and +/− 45° polarized antenna system, the proposed MIMO system shows the increase of channel capacity.

articleTitle: A two-stage optimization technique for multiband antenna design
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents an optimization technique aiming at multiband antenna design. The proposed method adopts the framework of multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, and a new mechanism balancing the degree of impedance matching and the degree of sufficient bandwidth is incorporated. Conventionally, the optimization of multiband antennas relies on either minimizing the maximum reflection coefficient or maximizing the area under the return-loss curve over targeted frequency bands. However, these methods direct an optimization algorithm to improper solution sub-domains in the multiband design problem. To overcome the limitation of conventional methods, the theoretical background of multiband optimization is investigated; furthermore, a two-stage optimizer is designed based on what the multiband optimization problem really needs. By using the proposed method, an internal multiband antenna for mobile communications covering 824–960 MHz and 1710–2170 MHz is successfully developed. The simulated and measured results show that the proposed technique outperforms the conventional approaches significantly.

articleTitle: Phase retrieval of scalar fields as a low number of sequential optimizations
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We propose a new and effective approach to the phase retrieval of scalar fields. In particular, we show that the problem can be conveniently tackled in terms of a low number of fast sequential optimizations. Numerical examples concerning the canonical case of far-field data and equispaced one-dimensional array antennas are provided in support of the given theory.

articleTitle: A fully planar substrate integrated probe-based wideband orthomode transducer
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper introduces a planar orthomode transducer (OMT) using substrate integrated waveguides (SIWs) and substrate integrated coaxial lines (SICLs) that is entirely contained within two substrate layers. SICLs form a quadruplet of probes inside the metal waveguide with fully symmetrical geometry. Such a structure is smaller and lighter than a waveguide OMT, its construction is simpler than of a coaxial OMT, however, isolation and loss properties are less degraded compared to the use of planar unshielded technologies such as microstrip. A new wideband inline SICL to SIW transition has been developed to allow grade separation of SIWs belonging to opposite polarizations through different substrate layers. The designed substrate integrated probe-based OMT on RO4003C<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">™</sup> substrate covers the frequency band from 8.1 GHz to 12.5 GHz with return loss higher than 19 dB, insertion loss less than 1.2 dB, inter-port isolation higher than 62 dB and cross-polarization discrimination higher than 65 dB.

articleTitle: Design of a high-gain millimeter-wave antenna using characteristic modes
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes the use of the Theory of Characteristic Modes to aid the design of high-gain antennas for mm-wave applications. A new lens antenna operating in the 19 to 22 GHz band is proposed. The lens consists of two metallic rings distributed in two layers and illuminated by a square aperture. The Theory of Characteristic Modes is used to analyze the proposed antenna in order to provide insight into the radiation characteristics of the structure. The proposed antenna has been optimized, obtaining a large bandwidth and a maximum directivity of 11.19 dBi at 22 GHz.

articleTitle: On feed line modifications for compact wideband antenna design
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Design of miniaturized wideband antennas is typically realized by introducing various geometrical modifications to the basic antenna topologies (e.g., monopoles or uniplanar structures). One of these modifications includes changing geometry of the feed line, either in a form of a taper or a stepped-impedance line. Here, systematic investigations on the effect of such modifications on obtainable size reduction ratio is carried out. We consider feed line modifications of various complexities (from two to six sections). In order to yield optimum designs, rigorous numerical optimization of relevant geometry parameters is executed. Numerical experiments are performed on two selected UWB monopoles and indicate advantage of the stepped-impedance feed line over the tapered one, as well as benefits of increasing the geometrical complexity of the line. At the same time, the results show the importance of simultaneous adjustment of all antenna parameters, necessary to exploit degrees of freedom of the feed line geometry.

articleTitle: Error control in MLFMA with multiple-precision arithmetic
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We present a new error control method that provides the truncation numbers as well as the required digits of machine precision for the translation operator of the multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA). The proposed method is valid for all frequencies, whereas the previous studies on error control are valid only for high-frequency problems (i.e., electrically large translation distances). When combined with a multiple-precision implementation of MLFMA, the proposed method can be used to solve low-frequency problems that are problematic with a fixed-precision implementation. Numerical results in the form of optimal truncation numbers and machine precisions for a variety of box sizes and desired relative error thresholds are presented and compared with the methods or numerical surveys available in the literature.

articleTitle: Versatile and accurate electromagnetic analysis of piecewise homogeneous composite objects
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The discretization by the Method of Moments (MoM) of electromagnetic integral equations, namely, the Electric Field Integral Equation (EFIE) for perfect electric conductors (PECs) and the Poggio-Miller-Chan-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) integral formulation for penetrable objects, is usually carried out with divergence-conforming sets of basis functions. However, in the single-surface analysis of piecewise homogeneous composite objects the implementation of divergence-conforming sets around junction-edges, where several regions intersect, becomes convoluted. Recently, the monopolar-RWG discretization, discontinuous at edges, of the EFIE and the PMCHWT formulation has been proposed. In this paper we show how this facet-based scheme becomes well suited for the single-surface analysis of piecewise homogeneous composite objects without giving special attention to junction-edges.

articleTitle: A smart and low-cost enhanced antenna system for industrial wireless broadband communication
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to investigate the traditional wireless local area network (LAN) deployment methods, challenges, and proposal of a novel smart antenna technique to mitigate the problems. In this paper, the focus is on the wireless link between cars to the road-side base station or trains to the trackside base station with fixed access point serving multiple mobile clients. A low-cost, highly scalable, long-range, half duplex hybrid smart antenna architecture with capability of direction of arrival (DOA) estimation and adaptive beamforming integration is proposed. The deployment cell size simulation result shows a drastic reduction in the number of equipment needed to cover the same service area as compared to the traditional method. The results will be of great importance for the future wireless deployment in the transportation market, knowing that the installation cost and maintenance cost are a major cost factor.

articleTitle: Accurate and low-dispersive control of refractive properties in fully metallic waveguides possessing twist symmetry
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We here present a method of reducing the dispersive nature of periodic structures by utilizing twist symmetries. A dispersion study of four different 1D periodic structures is conducted to present the advantage of structures possessing twist symmetries. The analysis shows a clearly reduced frequency dependence of twist-symmetric structures, compared to more simple periodic structures. Additional advantage provided by twist symmetries is the accurate control of the refractive properties of the structures. Promising applications of twist-symmetric guiding structures are leaky-wave antennas, filters and phase shifters.

articleTitle: Far-field radiation properties of lmpedance-loaded loop antennas from RF to optical frequencies
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Impedance loading of antennas has been of interest for more than half a century due to its ability to fundamentally change an antenna's operating characteristics. Variable reactive loading can be employed for configurability of the frequency response, polarization and far-field properties of an antenna. Closed-form expressions for the current and input impedance of a thin-wire loop antenna with loads in the periphery were derived in the RF and optical regimes in 1965 and 2017, respectively. Meanwhile, closed-form far-field radiation properties of circular loop antennas in the RF and optical regimes were derived in 1996 and 2017. This paper extends this theory to provide closed-form analytical expressions for the far-field radiation properties of impedance-loaded loop antennas valid from the RF to the optical regimes. The expressions are validated by comparison with commercial simulation tools. In addition, a beam steering example is presented as a potential application of the theory.

articleTitle: Investigation of the influence of build orientation on the surface roughness of the 3D metal printed horn antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This research presents the impact on surface roughness of build orientation in the fabrication of a 3D metal printed X-band horn antenna (8.2–12.4 GHz). Build orientation is investigated by printing the antenna at three different orientations of 45, 90 and 180, with respect to the building platform. The results indicate that the build orientation has an impact on the surface roughness, though not affecting its transmission coefficient in the X-band. The horn antennae are fabricated with Maraging Steel (MS1), using the Direct Metal Laser Sintering (DMLS) technique on an EOS M280 system. The variations in the microstructural surface roughness due to the build orientation are measured using a White Light Interferometer (WLI). The investigation proved that there is no significant effect of the orientation on the gain of the antenna while working in the X-band. However, the changes could be significant if working at higher frequencies, where this magnitude of surface roughness is more significant.

articleTitle: An in vivo exposure-system for wide-band electric pulses
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, the dosimetry of small animals arranged on a monopolar patch antenna for bioelectromagnetic experiments is reported. Numerical simulations were carried out to verify the matching of the antenna in the presence of a dielectric box to accommodate the small animals. This strategy, reducing the dielectric differences between the various irradiated materials, improves largely the efficiency of the setup. The induced electric field in the biological samples reached tens of V/m for an input voltage of 1 V, which is one of the highest efficiency obtained so far for these types of exposure setup. A very short electric pulse (on-time duration of 1 ns) is transferred mostly undistorted to the biological sample guaranteeing controlled experimental exposure conditions. Optimization of the positioning of the small animals was also analyzed. Our setup can be used to study effects of short and intense electric pulses in vivo only poorly addressed so far.

articleTitle: Support vector machines to accelerate reflectarray analysis and optimization
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The analysis of reflectarray antennas is substantially accelerated by using Support Vector Machines (SVMs) to model the matrix of reflection coefficients in substitution of a full-wave analysis based on local periodicity, the Method of Moments (MoM-LP) in this work. The SVM model takes as input variables two geometrical variables which control the phase-shift for two different polarizations. Thus, the employed model is able to analyze shaped-beam dual-linear polarized reflectarrays. As test case, a shaped-beam reflectarray radiating a pattern for Local Multipoint Distribution Service applications, presenting a squared-cosecant cut in elevation and sectored-beam in azimuth, is presented, showing a high degree of agreement in both the copolar and crosspolar patterns between the simulations of SVM and MoM-LP. Furthermore, the acceleration with regard to the MoM-LP is between three and four orders of magnitude, which demonstrates the suitability of the SVM model approach for reflectarray direct optimization.

articleTitle: Implementation of Rotman lens beamformer for relatively flexible multi-beam radiation control by electrically large phased arrays of antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper examines the implementation of Rotman lens beamformer to excite an electrically large phased array of antennas for multi-beam radiations. The goal is to relieve the number limitation of antenna ports arising from the limited surface profile of Rotman lens. Thus the confinement of sidelobe levels and beamwidths can be performed by increasing the array size and tapering the amplitudes of excitations. The radiation discrepancy due to the phase distortion by the defocused feeds will be also examined to justify the valid feeding area for orthogonal beamforming. Theoretical concepts will be first discussed with numerical examples shown to validate the feasibility and applicable scope.

articleTitle: Space-frequency propagator method for time-reversal imaging
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a novel propagator method (PM) for time reversal (TR) imaging is established. Based on simultaneous utilization of space-frequency (SF) multistatic scattering data matrix (MDM) acquired by large antenna arrays, the SF-PM algorithm has achieved a significant advantage of reduced computational complexity and better resolution compared with SF-multiple signal classification (SF-MUSIC) imaging method for the array with large number of sensors case. Numerical simulations verified the performance of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Statistics of rain attenuation in Prague, empirical data and numerical predictions
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Attenuation of electromagnetic waves in microwave bands is determined experimentally via measurement of received signal variations on terrestrial radio links operating in three frequency bands around 58, 94 and 122 GHz. The measured time series of attenuation are processed to obtain long-term cumulative distributions of attenuation due to hydrometeors. The obtained empirical distributions are compared with the ones predicted using the model of the Recommendation ITU-R P.530. For a given time percentages, the predicted attenuation levels exceeded are apparently lower than the levels of empirical distributions. A power-law relationship between attenuation and rain intensity is obtained by a least square approximation of measured simultaneous rain intensity and rain attenuation. The results are discussed and compared with the numerical predictions.

articleTitle: Compact dielectric filled septum polarizer feeder for a dual pol MTS antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper the design of a compact septum orthomode transducer polarizer working at Ku band is presented. The aim of this work is to design a feeding system to excite a rotationally symmetric MTS antenna with dual circularly polarized broadside radiation pattern. The proposed septum is composed by a stepped profile with 4 metallic steps, located in the center of a circular waveguide completely filled with a high permittivity material (AD1000 with dielectric constant 10.2). Total dimension of the proposed feeding system is 30 mm × 26.53 mm (1.31λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×1.16λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>). The structure is excited by two Teflon-based SMA connectors. The excitation of the input port determines right-hand or left-hand sense of the generated field. The OMT has been efficiently designed to obtain good reflection (−12 dB) and isolation (20 dB) parameters and the axial ratio at the output port is below 0.75 dB in all the working band.

articleTitle: Phantom study of a flat-faceted air-based microwave breast imaging system
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Imaging results obtained using a flat-faceted quasi-resonant air-based microwave breast imaging system are presented. These results are part of a phantom study wherein the imaging performance of the system is analyzed using various 3D breast phantoms. The phantoms are composed of three regions filled with fluids that mimick the dielectric properties of fat, fibroglandular, and tumour tissue. Full 3D images of the real and imaginary parts of the complex permittivity are produced using the Contrast Source Inversion algorithm with the electromagnetic modeling performed using either the FiniteElement or the Discontinuous Galerkin methods. Half-loop field probes are used to collect tangential magnetic-field data at various locations on the inner surface of the chamber. Air is used as the physical immersion medium but various inhomogeneous numerical backgrounds are utilized in the inversion model to regularize the mathematical problem. Single-frequency inversions are performed in the 0.9–2 GHz bandwidth. Tumour detection is used to measure imaging performance.

articleTitle: Nonradiating sources, cloaking devices and related anapole modes
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this work, theoretical findings on the common feature describing nonradiating sources is reported, based on equivalent sources from which it is possible to derive cloaking devices and anapole mode conditions. Starting from the differential form of Maxwell's Equations expressed in terms of equivalent electromagnetic sources, we derive two unique compact conditions. By specifing the nature of these passively induced or actively impressed current density sources in certain volumes and/or predefined surfaces, we derive theoretical results consistently with the literature about nonradiating particles, cloaking devices and anapole mode structures through peculiar destructive interactions between volumetric-volumetric, volumetric-surface and surface-surface equivalent sources.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized brick-wall nantenna array for optical communications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a circularly polarized nano-antenna array with a new topology. The array is composed of two orthogonal brick-wall sub-arrays each of which is constructed from six parallel radiators connected via narrow rods. To achieve circular polarization, the two sub-arrays are excited with 90° phase difference between them. The proposed array is characterized by its high directivity and wide axial-ratio bandwidth covering the range from 188.2 THz to 197.8 THz with around 83% radiation efficiency at its central frequency. These radiation characteristics are considered very attractive for optical communication applications.

articleTitle: Exploiting the aperture antennas theory in the assessment of orbital angular momentum antennas limitations in far-field links
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We exploit the classical Aperture Antennas Theory as a simple tool for the analysis of OAM antennas' performances in far-field links. The outcomes are supported by the observation of the singular values of the radiation operator and include the analytical determination of the number of degrees of freedom of the radiated field associated to each vortex.

articleTitle: Manufacturable ultra-thin resistive FSS for challenging EM mobile environments
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper reports on recent developments in the manufacture and measured electromagnetic (EM) performance of a new class of thin microwave absorbers based on metal backed resistively loaded Frequency Selective Surfaces (FSS). Ink jet printing technology is shown to be a viable method for creating patterned FSS elements very close to the desired resistance values. This is demonstrated by comparing simulated and measured reflectivity plots for an ink jet and a stencil printed polarisation independent absorber that is designed to work in the frequency range 7.1–24 GHz. Numerical simulations show that thin FSS absorbers provide radar backscatter suppression, not only in the far field of the illuminating antenna, but also when the EM source is placed very close to the surface of the periodic array. This technology can therefore provide a solution for enhancing the performance of wireless sensors placed close to lossy loads such as the human body.

articleTitle: A wideband CPW-fed stepped monopole slot antenna for 5G communications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a super wide-band planar monopole slot antenna for 5G mobile communication bands from 22.97-35.04 GHz. The proposed antenna has a planar slot with a stepped monopole structure at its center that is fed through a Coplanar waveguide. The antenna has a peak gain of 5.7 dBi and radiation efficiency greater than 98%. The proposed antenna has a size of 8×8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. An 8-element array configuration of the antenna provides maximum absolute gain of 14.9 dBi. The antenna array has an overall size of 8×64 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Radiation patterns of the array has 3dB beam-width of as narrow as 9.2 degrees with side lobe level of -13.1 dB. The large bandwidth, high gain and small size of this antenna makes it a potential candidate for future 5G mobile phones and millimeter-wave communications.

articleTitle: W-band high-gain low profile circularly polarized magneto-electric dipole antenna array with gap waveguide feeding technology
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain circularly polarized (CP) aperture-coupled magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna array excited by the air cavity in gap waveguide (GWG) feeding technology in W-band is proposed. This antenna array is composed of two layers, upper CP ME-dipole antenna subarrays and lower metallic GWG feeding networks. The planar antenna array structure is realized by the high mode air cavity feeding network, which is realized by extending the 1×2 cavity to 3×2 cavity using more shorted pins to split the electromagnetic field. The whole single-layer GWG feeding network is composed of a ridge gap waveguide (RGWG) transmission structure and short-ended vertical polarized groove gap waveguide (VP-GGWG) high mode air cavities. The transmission loss caused by the coupling and the fabrication tolerance can be reduced by combining the RGWG and GGWG in the same layer. In addition, the feeding network is fabricated all in metal with no substrate loss. Transverse slots are etched at the right position of the printed circuit board (PCB) backside to excite the CP ME-dipoles. The antenna element has stable radiation patterns and wide axialratio (AR) bandwidth. The proposed 3×8 planner antenna array has a maximum boresight gain of 22 dBi and an AR bandwidth of 10.8% for AR <;; 3 dB. In the frequency band from 87.7 to 97.7 GHz, a boresight gain above 20 dBi is achieved.

articleTitle: Electronically steerable circularly polarized planar antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a steerable, circularly polarized planar antenna operating at 2.45 GHz. The design employs a central omni-directional circularly polarized active element surrounded by electronically controllable parasitic elements that are used to steer the beam in the desired direction. The proposed antenna is capable of steering the beam in an arbitrary direction. The antenna has a 3 dB gain and an axial ratio of less than 2 dB in the direction of radiation.

articleTitle: Establishing the limits of antenna measurement in fading channels
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper explains how antennas and channels can be characterized from only one S-parameter measurement in a fading channel. This also allows designers to obtain the transfer function (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) of an antenna if an anechoic chamber is not available. The procedure is to characterize an antenna and a channel by using the S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> measurement between two identical antennas in a fading channel. The antenna and channel responses in the time domain were separated from the time response of the measured S21. This is then used to determine the response of the antenna and the channel in the frequency domain. The S21 of the antenna obtained from the procedure is compared with those of measurements obtained in an anechoic chamber. Good agreement between the two results is obtained. The procedure was validated using a wideband and narrowband antenna to establish the limits of the measurement in fading channels.

articleTitle: High order description of complex geometries for integral equation methods in electromagnetic scattering problems
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper shows a new technique to produce infinitely differentiable geometries from a finite set of control points. The technique is used in other communities (computer graphics) and will be very useful for the implementation of high order integral equation methods in computational electromagnetics. In this paper we show the 2D case (curves) and show some examples of a possible extension to surfaces in 3D. Along the process we construct a discrete set of points on the smooth geometry together with weights, normal and tangent vectors that allow us to discretize to high order any integral on that geometry.

articleTitle: Correction for transition boundary conditions to consider scattering by a chiral infinite slab
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, the reflection and transmission problem from chiral slab is investigated. The chiral slab is simulated by the transition boundary conditions (TBCs) to reduce the complexity of the problem. The oblique incidence case is considered.
