publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The feasibility of using a textile fastener (Velcro) for the implementation of a practical interconnection of a wearable all-textile stripline has been studied through measurements with experimental prototypes. The derived results demonstrate acceptable performance in terms of power transfer attenuation. Long and short textile transmission lines (striplines) may be required to be flexibly connected and disconnected in wearable applications e.g. patient monitoring. The use of Velcro can enable and increase the chances for the above requirements to be met.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable circularly polarized cross-dipole antenna with a near-field resonant parasitic element
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a polarization switchable circularly polarized (CP) antenna that consists of a compact single-feed crossed dipole loaded with a near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) element. This antenna is placed above a metallic reflector to enhance its gain and broadside radiation pattern. A meander line with an arrowhead-shaped ending was applied to all arms of the crossed dipole and NFRP elements for compactness. By adjusting the end size of the NFRP element, the antenna was capable of switching its polarization from right-hand circular polarization to left-hand circular polarization and vice versa. The reconfigurability is realized by controlling the ON/OFF states of 8 PIN-diodes, which are inserted into the arrowhead endings of the NFRP element. For the RHCP mode, the antenna yields a |S11| <;; -10 dB bandwidth of 1.465-1.665 GHz and a 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth of 1.535-1.590 GHz. For the LHCP mode, the antenna yields a |S11| <;; -10 dB bandwidth of 1.50-1.69 GHz and a 3-dB AR bandwidth of 1.545-1.585 GHz. Moreover, in both modes, the antenna yields a good broadside radiation pattern with a gain of > 6.0 dBic and a radiation efficiency of > 70% across its operational bandwidth.

articleTitle: Accelerating a ray launching model using GPU with CUDA
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The high computational cost of accurate deterministic wave propagation models often prevent them from being used in channel modelling. In this work, we present our experience of attempts to accelerate our 2.5D ray launching model using GPUs (Graphic Processing Units), which continue to grow in popularity due to their vast computation capability. At the heart of this trial is an implementation of a ray-surface intersection detection function, which was found to be the bottleneck of serial CPU computation, using NVIDIA's CUDA (Compute Unified Device Architecture). Various optimization efforts are made to obtain the best overall performance. The intersection detection function executes seven times faster on a large urban scenario after acceleration on a modest laptop GPU. This paper details the implementation of the CUDA-based intersection detection function and presents the acceleration results for different simulated environments.

articleTitle: Exploring the next generation of array receivers and signal processing systems for radio astronomy
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Arrays for radio astronomy are challenging to build and operate due to their sheer size and data volume, but also due to the high expectations on signal fidelity and performance in challenging environments. This paper explores some of the next generation technology applicable to large antenna arrays, using the Square Kilometre Array (SKA) as an example. Fundamental components of these arrays are receivers for each signal path and the signal processing performed on these signals.

articleTitle: Low-cost multi-objective optimization of antennas by means of generalized Pareto ranking bisection algorithm
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper introduces a generalized Pareto ranking bisection algorithm for low-cost multi-objective design optimization of antenna structures. The algorithm allows for identifying a set of Pareto optimal sets of parameters (that represent the best trade-offs between considered objectives) by iterative partitioning of the intervals connecting previously found designs and executing a Pareto-ranking-based poll search. The initial approximation of the Pareto front found using the bisection procedure is subsequently refined to the level of the high-fidelity EM model of the antenna at hand using local optimization. A serious limitation of the original bisection algorithm was that only two objectives could be considered. The generalized version proposed here allows for handling any number of design goals. An improved poll search procedure has also been developed and incorporated. Our algorithm has been demonstrated using an example of a UWB monopole antenna with three figures of interest taken into account: structure size, reflection response, and gain variability.

articleTitle: Hybrid technique for efficient and accurate analysis of the V2X channel in urban traffic scenarios
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: It is presented a new hybrid technique combining Method of Moments, Physical Optics and Geometrical Theory of Diffraction for the analysis of the vehicle to vehicle and vehicle to infraestructure radio-wave channel in urban traffic scenes. The technique is efficient and accurate for solving the electrically large and multiscale problem that appears in the analyses of these channels. Representative results and cross validations are presented.

Author Keywords: vehicle to vehicle and vehicle to infraestructure radio-channels

articleTitle: Distributed OFDM transmitter scheme for Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a new type of distributed orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) transmitter architecture, which can be used in the Internet of Things (IoT) networks with distributed sensor nodes, where the nodes are required to send different data back to the hub simultaneously. The sub-carrier settings for analogue OFDM modulation across the entirety of the distributed sensor network are enabled by a broadcasted two-tone signal. The performance of the proposed two-tone sub-carrier synchronization approach is evaluated under different two-tone signal to noise ratios (SNRs). Furthermore, system bit error rates (BERs) are simulated for various sub-carrier frequency offsets and transmitter settings, in order to provide guidelines for practical system designs.

articleTitle: Flexibility in multi-beam satellite antennas: Requirements, challenges and solutions
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Multi-beam antennas come in a number of forms, systems and configurations. As telecommunication satellite operators look to provide service to a variety of applications, minimise risk, maximize fill rate and efficiency, flexibility has become an increasing requirement. However, with flexibility comes additional complexities and challenges. This paper looks at the requirements that are now being asked of multi-beam antennas in terms of flexibility of resources, challenges in terms of design, analysis and testing and looks into example solutions that have been found in answering such challenges. As industry looks to advanced systems that include digital processors and digital beamforming such considerations will play an increasingly important role.

articleTitle: Modified Kirchhoff diffraction of pulsed EM waves radiated from a slot-excited Fabry-Perot resonator antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Diffraction of pulsed electromagnetic (EM) waves in a slot excited Fabry Perot type resonator antenna is studied analytically in the modified Kirchhoff approximation. Closed-form space-time expressions for the radiated EM fields are found using the Cagniard-DeHoop technique. Illustrative numerical examples are given.

articleTitle: Design of UHF RFID tag antenna for automotive tire
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a novel UHF RFID Tag antenna for automotive tire is presented. The antenna shape and size are optimized by using a meander line. To achieve a proper impedance matching between the antenna and the microchip a T-match is performed. The square-load is added at its ends to improve the bandwidth. The tag has a reduced size: 80mm×12mm×1.6mm. Hence, it can be attached simply in automotive tire. The tag provides the simple and low cost fabrication. The simulated results show that the impedance matching is very convenient with broad impedance bandwidth. Moreover, the proposed antenna has omnidirectional radiation patterns and appreciable gain that satisfy maximum power transmitting in RFID communication.

articleTitle: Multiband antenna operation with a non-resonant element using a reconfigurable matching network
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A small non-resonant antenna element (86.4mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>) is proposed for multiband operation in combination with a reconfigurable matching network. The non-resonant antenna element is in the corner of a ground plane, featuring representative dimensions (120 mm × 60 mm) of a wireless device such as a smartphone. Said reconfigurable matching network uses a variable capacitor implemented with MEMS technology having a small footprint of only 2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. A particular capacitance value is selected through a digital input allowing 32 states. For the present case, only four states are enough in order to cover the frequency range of 698MHz–960MHz up to 1710MHz–2690MHz. Measured average total efficiencies across the bands are above 40% making the solution attractive for multiband wireless devices.

articleTitle: Initial Ku-band air-ground channel measurement results
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) are growing in use, hence many organizations are at work on investigations to make these systems safe and reliable. For UAS that are beyond range of a ground station, communication by satellite is envisioned. For such airsatellite links, different frequency bands are under consideration, and one of these is the Ku band. To allow UAS to use the Ku band requires that existing Ku band systems not suffer interference from UAS transmissions. Terrestrial fixed (point-to-point) services are a primary concern for such interference. Thus to help regulatory authorities determine the feasibility of UAS use of the Ku band, and to help determine possible constraints on such use, NASA Glenn Research Center has conducted flight tests to gather data for development of some Ku band air-ground propagation models. This paper describes these flight tests, and provides some preliminary results. As expected, propagation path loss is reasonably well-approximated by free space, yet for interference coordination, high accuracy in attenuation modeling is desired. This requires careful alignment of the extremely narrow beam fixed service antennas, accurate representation of aircraft attitude, and incorporation of precise antenna pattern and flight geometric information. This analysis is ongoing, with Ku band propagation path loss models expected as future work.

articleTitle: Realizable source that radiates the field of a Hertzian dipole with complex source point
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The radiation from a Hertzian dipole with a source point in complex space (called a complex dipole) has very unusual properties: the field in the near zone closely resembles the farfield pattern, which has no sidelobes and exhibits exponential decay away from a main-beam direction. The inverse source problem for the complex dipole is formulated for non-resonant arrays with reactive zones that do not extend significantly beyond the physical dimensions of the array. A closed-form expression is given for the minimum size that such a non-resonant source must have to radiate the pattern of a complex dipole. This minimum size depends on the accuracy required. Using a least-squares approach, an array of orthogonal Hertzian dipoles in real space is constructed to radiate the far-field pattern of a single complex dipole. The physical dimension of the array can be smaller than the diameter of the branch-cut disk of the complex dipole.

articleTitle: Impact of fibroblast cell density on the material parameters of thin artificial human skin in the terahertz band
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the material parameters of collagen gel and dermal equivalents with different fibroblast cell densities in a Terahertz (THz) band from 0.2 THz to 1.5 THz. It is shown that collagen gel without cells has much higher refractive index and absorption coefficient than dermal equivalents, while the parameters of dermal equivalents slightly decrease with cell density. It denotes that the material parameters at the THz band is not only dependent on the water concentration but also their intrinsic biological features. The obtained results help understand the interaction of the THz wave with biological tissues and the diversity of material parameters of real human skin.

articleTitle: W-band true-time delay phase shifters using paraffin microactuators
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We report a distributed loaded line phase shifter based on a new class of electro-thermally actuated RF MEMS devices using paraffin phase-change material (PCM). Paraffin is a low loss (tan δ = 6.6 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup>) mechanical phase-change material that exhibits a 15% volumetric change through its solid-liquid transition. Due to its unique electrical and mechanical properties, paraffin PCM variable capacitors exhibit a very low loss which is critical in designing reconfigurable structures. Here, a low-loss paraffin PCM based true-time delay, continuously-tunable phase shifter is designed and optimized. A figure-of merit of 71.8°/dB is achieved while maintaining a return loss more than 12 dB. Designed phase shifter has a maximum insertion loss of 5 dB for a 360° phase shift. Electro-thermo-mechanical performance of the paraffin PCM device is studied by carrying out a fully coupled multiphysics simulation. Maximum displacement of 0.8 μm is achieved with a 2.6 μm-thick paraffin film. A new fabrication method for the deposition of the thin paraffin film is developed and a fabrication process for the device is presented.

articleTitle: Phase sensitivity of the projection method for a beam tilting deformed array
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Antenna arrays laid on surfaces that change shape in time are widely employed in modern wireless communication devices. An issue related to the design of these antenna systems is the control of the radiation pattern, whose shape results to be distorted as a consequence of the surface deformation. The projection method is a simple and cost-effective technique that allows to retrieve the pattern of deformed arrays, by using uniquely a set of phase shifters. As the resolution desired for a phase shifter can impact considerably on its cost, a preliminary study about the actual minimum phase step required can support the designer when purchasing the equipment for an experimental setup. In this work we make an analytical study, supported by CST simulations, on the approximation that can be made on the phase correction to be applied to an 1 χ 4 half-wedge-deformed array.

articleTitle: Coplanar multiband antenna on flexible substrate in energy harvesting system for IOT applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a flexible multi-band antenna that operates at telecommunication frequencies using a coplanar waveguide approach for energy harvesting system for IoT applications. Despite the compact size, the measured results show an antenna gain of 1.37 at 900 MHz, 4.16 at 1800 MHz and 6.15 at 2.6 GHz. To cope with the form factor of packaging and objects, the antenna can be bent in a cylinder form of radius 14 mm or be folded into a rectangular dimension 30 mm × 27 mm without changing the resonant frequencies. The deformation degrades the antenna gain by less than 2 dB compared to the flat structure. The simulation and measurement results of the proposed design are consistent.

articleTitle: A novel low-profile wideband reconfigurable CP antenna array
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: For future wireless communications, cost-effective, low-profile circular polarization (CP) antennas with wide bandwidth and high directivity are highly desirable to increase system capacity and suppress polarization mismatch. In this paper, a wideband circular polarization antenna array integrated with a polarization-independent artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) is reported that meets the demands. First, a wideband CP reconfigurable antenna with a pair of cross-bowtie radiators and a metal ground is presented to achieve a fractional bandwidth of 35.9%. By replacing the metal ground with a polarization-independent AMC ground, the antenna profile is reduced from 0.25λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> to 0.05λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub> with only a slight bandwidth decrease. A wideband CP reconfigurable 4-element linear array is achieved using four of those elements. It is low profile (0.05 λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>), and has a wide operating bandwidth (21.7%), and a high realized gain (13 dBic).

articleTitle: A wide band compact size UHF band monopole clustered with L and S band dipoles for self-networking communication in handset devices
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A wide band monopole antenna that works at Ultrahigh frequency (UHF) clustered with two wide band dipole antennas that work at L and S band are proposed in this paper. The three antennas are in the cover of a handset device which connects to the ground plane on its main body with a wire. The UHF monopole antenna covers the frequency band from 350 MHz to 780 MHz with VSWR lower than 3 in a total length of 0.16λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with omnidirectional gain upon 0 dBi which is used for self-networking communication. The L band dipole antenna shares part of the ground plane with the UHF monopole antenna, which works from 1.23 GHz to 1.62 GHz, with the end fire gain upon 6 dBi. The S band dipole antenna covers from 1.7 GHz to 2.34 GHz with gain upon 6 dBi. The three antennas have good isolation higher than 15 dB. The simulation indicates that the proposed clustered antennas have small volume, stable radiation pattern and wide band.

articleTitle: Bacterial detection by using micro immunosensing biomedical cavity resonator
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Micro immuno-sensors are used for rapid detection of different bacteria in medical samples. Salmonella is a bacteria that acts as a major cause of illness throughout the world. Mobile microwave biosensor system is used to determine bacteria pathogens in medical samples as well as in liquids. The biosensor device described here is a portable selfstanding user friendly that can be used for detection in the field. The sensor chip is a rectangular slot coupled feed circular microstrip cavity disc antenna designed to operate at industrial scientific and medical (ISM 2.45 GHz) frequency band. The sensor design is done by using two substrates, first one is the fixed feeding mechanism substrata and second substrate is circular movable patch. The studies of the change of electrical properties of serum samples are presented to detect different concentrations of salmonella. By this system we examined the existence of salmonella as a bacterium. Each bacterium resembles unique phase pattern that helps in its identifications of the samples.

articleTitle: All-metal dual frequency RHCP high gain antenna for the extreme environments of a Europa Lander
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A new all-metal dual-frequency RHCP high gain antenna is under development at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory for the potential Europa Lander mission. The antenna is mainly made of metal to survive the harsh environment conditions (i.e. very low temperature and high radiation and ESD levels). The antenna is also flat to meet drastic volume constraints and has efficiencies higher than 80% at both the uplink and downlink X-band Deep Space frequency bands. This antenna is a key component to the mission enabling Direct Link to Earth (DTE) from and Direct-from-Earth (DFE) to the lander without any relay.

articleTitle: Compensation method for distorted active phased array antennas in condition of quantization errors based on structural-electromagnetic coupling
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Widely used digital attenuator and phase shifter could inevitably introduce quantization errors for distorted active phased array antenna, at the time of controlling the amplitude and phase for improving the electromagnetic performance. The reduction of quantization errors decides the compensation effect for antenna in complex service environment. Therefore, a compensation method for distorted antenna in condition of quantization errors is presented based on the coupled structural-electromagnetic model with least squares method. The quantized amplitude and phase adjustments are deduced from the perspective of multiple dividing of minimum quantization value and the optimal amplitude and phase differences, which could be implemented to recover a high quality pattern from a distorted antenna. Lastly, an X-band active phased array antenna with representative saddle shape deformation is illustrated to verify the compensation effect for quantization errors including both the amplitude and phase.

articleTitle: A novel clustering method based on density peaks and its validation by channel measurement
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, cluster centers are defined as local maxima in the density which is called density peaks. We use an algorithm based on density peaks to cluster multipath components (MPCs) whose parameters are estimated by the space-alternating generalized expectation-maximization (SAGE) algorithm. To validate its performance, we apply it to the data from a channel measurement in an indoor scenario at 28 GHz and compare it to the widely used KPowerMeans algorithm with the same distance metric of multiple component distance (MCD). Through the results, we find it can cluster MPCs more accurately validated by Calinski-Harabasz (CH) and Davies-Bouldin (DB) indices. More importantly, it overcomes the shortcoming of setting the number of clusters manually because we can determine the cluster centers automatically. Besides, the efficiency of DP clustering is far superior to KPowerMeans because what it needs is only a distance matrix and we only need to compute it once. At the end, statistical analysis of clusters are presented to provide insights in channel modeling of millimeter wave.

articleTitle: Study on curved barrier to reduce electromagnetic interference from solid cables
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper shows electromagnetic analysis on the design of a curved barrier to prevent electromagnetic interference (EMI) from a solid cable in nuclear power plants. We investigate the regulatory guidance applied to nuclear power plants to prevent electromagnetic (EM) problems, which are the malfunction and degradation of digital equipment. Based on the investigated regulatory guide, we electrostatically analyze the curved EM barrier using a mode-matching method in conjunction with the superposition principle. Using the series solution obtained by the mode-matching method, we derive the distribution of the electric-field strength and the capacitance per unit length while varying the geometric parameters of the curved EM barrier. The results in this paper provide us with useful information to reduce undesirable EMI from a solid cable.

articleTitle: Microwave measurements of high dielectric constant ceramics by powder mixture equations — A further study
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The measurements of the real parts (dielectric constants) of complex permittivity of composite samples at microwave frequencies made by titanium dioxide ceramic filler dispersed in the polyethylene matrix are studied in this research. The dielectric constant of pure ceramic was deduced from the experimental dielectric constants of composites under different filler percentages by mixture equations. The titanium dioxide ceramic has a dielectric constant of 100 at microwave frequencies. Five well known mixture equations and a newly published mixture equation which was derived from one of the five equations were adopted in this study. The matching condition of the six mixing equations with measured dielectric constant values of the mixtures was investigated. The theoretical errors of various equations for the calculation of dielectric constant of pure ceramic were derived and studied. The best candidate equation for measuring the dielectric constants of pure ceramic materials is then suggested.

articleTitle: Hybrid simulations with measurements as improved technique to obtain the complex antenna responses on structures
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: With the growth of multiple antenna systems (SIMO, MIMO), the knowledge of the complex antenna responses have to be obtained with a good accuracy to be used in the vector signal processing step. However these responses may depend on the structure where antennas are integrated. Furthermore, these structures completely change between terrestrial, naval or aerial applications. Actual techniques to obtain antenna responses are mainly based on measurements and are often limited or complex in the case of integration over a non-trivial structure (building, vehicle, plane, boat …). An emergent technique is to hybridized measurements and simulations to obtain the desired accurate data.

articleTitle: Towards performance optimisation of the FDTD method via matrix casting approach
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This publication presents matrix casting approach for the FDTD method. Applied in 2D and 3D dimensions it is subsequently parallelised with OpenMP and tested in basic air-filled and realistic landmine-detection scenarios.

articleTitle: Design tools for small implantable antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Implantable applications have been increasing in number in an exponential manner since the turn of the millennium. This is largely due to the increasing availability of ultra low power consumption electronics, enabling the emergence of healthcare services using implantable or swallowable sensors. Other fields of applications exist, e.g. in the domains of military, security or sports. A large number of antennas for these implantable or swallowable capsules have been designed, and can be found in the literature. They are however always presented for a specific capsule and application, and are thus very difficult to compare in terms of antenna characteristics. In this paper, we show results obtained for simple canonical implantable radiation sources, obtained using a specifically developed numerical tool presented earlier. These canonical results will allow us to obtain some simple but useful figures of merit that enable an easy assessment of the quality of the radiation characteristic of a specific antenna design in a specific capsule.

articleTitle: On the use of a metasurface prism in gap-waveguide technology to reduce the dispersion of leaky-wave antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Leaky-wave antennas (LWAs) feature the advantages of high directivity, wide impedance bandwidth, and their ability to scan with frequency. However, the dispersive beam-scanning makes the LWAs very difficult to be utilized in systems that require high-speed data transfer, wide band and high directive antennas. This paper proposes a simple but effective method to reduce the dispersion of LWAs by loading with a metasurface prism realized in gap-waveguide technology. Naturally combining the two technologies, a leaky-wave gap waveguide antenna and a dispersive prism, a low-dispersive gap-waveguide leaky-wave antenna is achieved, with a specific radiation direction that in this example is ϕ= 41°. The main radiation direction varies only ±0.5° from 11.5 to 13.0 GHz, with side-lobe levels lower than −13 dB. A 20% half-power gain-drop frequency bandwidth has been obtained. The realized gain varies from 16.4 to 16.8 dBi with a narrow half-power beamwidth of 5°. The full-wave simulations in HFSS agree well with the theoretical calculations.

articleTitle: Radiation characteristics of EWE antenna on actual ground for landslides prediction based on bistatic radar system using AM radio broadcasting
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The complex permittivities of the hydrated soil have been measured and the transmission characteristics of the electromagnetic wave in air-hydrated soil boundary have been calculated as the first step of the realization of the landslides prediction system so far. Consequently, it becomes obvious that the reflected wave from the hydrated soil increases as the water content increases and the transmitting wave decreases until it is difficult to measure. Keeping this results in mind, the antenna called EWE at operating frequency of 1MHz has been investigated in order to measure the reflected wave from lands in this paper. The miniaturization and the influence of the conductivity of the ground have been considered.

articleTitle: Model for the evaluation of the loss tangent of a dielectric material with a scanning split-ring resonator probe
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Recently an approach for fast quantitative surface scanning of dielectric permittivity at microwave frequency using a single split ring resonator (SRR) was presented [1]. While an analytical solution for retrieving the dielectric permittivity from raw measurement data was developed and experimentally verified, the quantification of the dielectric loss evaluated using the same technique remains an unsolved problem. Here we propose a model for estimation of the complex dielectric properties of materials from the experimental measurements of the transmission coefficient determined by the SRR probe. The relative permittivity and the loss tangent of a dielectric substrate are evaluated from the resonant frequency and Q-factor of the SRR probe placed in contact with the substrate. The response of the SRR test probe is related theoretically to the complex permittivity by considering an equivalent circuit in terms of the capacitance and radiation resistance of the SRR.

articleTitle: Low-profile circularly-polarized filtering antenna with improved bandwidth and gain
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel circularly-polarized (CP) microstrip antenna with a low profile, broad bandwidth, high gain and filtering characteristics is presented. The antenna has a resonator-based vertically coupled structure, which consists of a patch, an embedded slot resonator and a hairpin resonator. Such a structure can effectively broaden the impedance bandwidth without increasing the profile of the antenna. The CP characteristics are achieved by employing a single-fed dual-coupled feeding technique that an intrinsic and broadband 90<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> phase difference can be realized between the two coupling paths. This CP technique effectively excites the TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf>-mode of the patch without using any power dividers and phase delay lines, resulting in the reduction of circuit complexity and insertion loss, and therefore the improved gain response. In addition, owing to the coupled resonant structures, the antenna exhibits the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>-order filtering features with improved impedance and axial ratio (AR) bandwidths, flat in-band gain and out-of-band rejection. The measured results verify the design, showing an impedance bandwidth of 29.6%, and 3-dB AR bandwidth of 17.6%. The antenna also exhibits a high gain of over 9.5 dBic.

articleTitle: Fading characterization of UE to ceiling-mounted access point communications at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation of the first- and second-order statistics of the small-scale fading observed in short range indoor millimeter-wave channels between a user equipment (UE) and a ceiling-mounted access point (AP) operating at 60 GHz. In this study, three UE positions associated with common use cases were considered: making a voice call (head), sending a text message or operating an app (hand) and carrying a device (pocket). For the mobile line of sight (LOS) and nonLOS (NLOS) channel measurements, the user walked towards and away from the AP within an indoor hallway environment. The first- and second-order statistics of the Rice and Nakagami-m fading models were employed to characterize the small-scale fading behavior experienced in the UE-to-AP channels. Overall, they were shown to provide a good agreement with the measured channel data. Using the Akaike information criterion, the Nakagami-m distribution was favored for the majority of the cases considered in this study.

articleTitle: Ray-tracing simulations and millimeter wave massive MIMO performance evaluation for rail traffic scenarios
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a practical study on the influence of scenarios on millimeter wave massive MIMO performance evaluation and optimal number of train access points at 60GHz band. The specification on the path loss model is developed for six rail traffic scenario modules. In particular, we prove that the channel parameters used for millimeter wave massive MIMO performance evaluation and optimal number of train access points should be deterministic and accurate. Finally, the simulation results imply that the influence of different scenarios should be evaluated when verifying millimeter wave massive MIMO for future rail traffic communications.

articleTitle: Uneven-layered metamaterial tile for ultra-wideband RCS reduction
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a novel uneven-layered metamaterial tile is proposed for ultra-wideband radar cross section (RCS) reduction. The metamaterial tile is composed of two kinds of square ring unit cells with different layer thickness. The reflection phase difference of 180° (±37°) between two unit cells covers an ultra-wide frequency range. The metamaterial tile can achieve −10 dB RCS reduction from 6.2 GHz to 25.7 GHz with the ratio bandwidth of 4.15:1 at normal incidence. The measured and simulated results are in good agreement and validate the proposed uneven-layered metamaterial tile can greatly expanding the bandwidth for RCS reduction.

articleTitle: Frequency-reconfigurable pattern-steerable antenna using active frequency selective surface
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A brief review of reconfigurable frequency selective surfaces is presented in this paper, with emphasis on practical biasing techniques. Several important properties of the design techniques are summarized. Two case studies are given for single layer active frequency selective surface using a slot type unit cell, as well as integration of a feed antenna to realize a frequency-tunable pattern reconfigurable antenna. The measured performance of the resulting antenna is presented to verify the design concept. Exploiting active frequency selective surfaces opens up new methods to design reconfigurable antennas.

articleTitle: Enhanced cooperative spectrum sensing in hybrid homogeneous-heterogeneous cognitive radio networks
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an enhanced cooperative spectrum sensing (CSS) for Hybrid Homogeneous-Heterogeneous Cognitive Radio Networks (HCRNs) which utilizes (i) the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) to evaluate the degree of reliability, and (ii) the reporting time to merges as a flexible sensing time in order to evaluate spectrum sensing more accurately. Before making a global decision based on the Dempster-Shafer (D-S) theory at the Fusion Centre (FC), the flexible sensing time is applied to adopt its sensing data. Simulation results show that our proposed scheme achieves better detection gain than conventional schemes.

articleTitle: Recent progress of incidence angle-insensitive broadband metamaterial absorbers
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper introduces the recent progress of incidence angle- and polarization-insensitive broadband metamaterial (MM) absorbers. The polarization insensitivity can be easily achieved by a symmetric geometry. In order to achieve incidence angle insensitivity, a unique unit cell must be designed. In this paper, we introduced three angle insensitive unit cells for metamaterial absorber applications. In order to achieve broadband absorption, we introduced two approaches such as multi-resonance and resistive patterns based on the angle- and polarization-insensitive MM absorbers. Therefore, we presented three angle- and polarization-insensitive broadband metamaterial (MM) absorbers.

articleTitle: High power non-foster circuit class-J GaN HEMT amplifier
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes high power non-Foster circuit Class-J GaN HEMT amplifier. The non-Foster circuit (NFC) cancels the transistor parasitic capacitance thereby sustaining the bandwidth and enhancing the output power, efficiency and gain in the scale of Class AB PA. The power amplifier (PA) was designed based on Cree's CGHV40030F packaged GaN HEMT biased with drain supply voltage of 60V at quiescent drain-to-source current of 21mA. The GaN HEMTs in the NFC were biased with drain supply voltage of 20V at quiescent drain-to-source current of 3mA. This keeps the NFC to PA transistor biasing ratio at 1:3. The PA operates from 4.2 to 4.4 GHz with center frequency of 4.3 GHz. The NFC effective negative capacitance ranges from −1.7 to −45.6 pF. The effective negative capacitance at 4.3 GHz stood at −1.9 pF. The PA has 50% drain efficiency, 46.1% power added efficiency (PAE), 43 dBm output power and 11 dB transducer power gain.

articleTitle: Implementation of FDTD waveguide port based on virtual domain
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The waveguide port for finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) method is implemented by virtual domain. The virtual domain is not contained in the main domain and is used to absorb wave through the communication between inner main domain and virtual domain. In this way, the spatial restriction of the waveguide uniform feeding part before the discontinuity is further relaxed. Through the specially designed communication, the feeding plane behaves as PEC boundary for outer main domain and guide wave, without any reflection between virtual domain and inner main domain, with conformal algorithm naturally contained. Numerical result of a dielectric-loaded waveguide with a very short feeding part validates the proposed implementation for waveguide port.

articleTitle: A wideband multi-beam yagi based MIMO antenna system with multiple parasitic directors
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A proof of concept design for splitting the single conventional beam of a Yagi antenna into multiple beams is presented by exciting the 3λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> loop resonating mode as well as using multiple director elements. The proposed multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system is designed in a triangular configuration, so that the adjacent beams do not cancel the effect of each other and to achieve orthogonal radiation patterns each covering 120<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">o</sup> sector. The design has a minimum measured −10 dB bandwidth of 980 MHz (5.66–6.64 GHz) targeting the WLAN band. The board diameter of the MIMO antenna system is only 120 mm. It has a minimum front-to-back ratio (FBR) of 10 dB, gain of 3.8 dBi, and efficiency of 92%. The proposed MIMO antenna system has high port isolation of 30 dB and low envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) value of 0.012 in the entire band of operation between all its elements.

articleTitle: A millimeter-wave dual-circularly-polarized microstrip antenna array with a novel single feed network
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A dual-circularly-polarized (DCP) patch antenna array with a novel substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) feed network is proposed at millimeter-wave band. In our design, two polarizations share a common feed network and radiation elements so that the two polarizations have very similar performance. To demonstrate the working principle of the proposed structure, an 8×8-element array is designed and fabricated. The array shows a wide bandwidth (SWR<2, AR<3) of 24%, a maximum gain of about 25.8 dBic, and a port-to-port isolation larger than 14 dB.

articleTitle: Example antenna and link performance for wireless network on chip applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Wireless networks on chips, or WiNoCs, are being investigated as supplemental methods to support the very high data rates required of future multi-core integrated circuits. These WiNoCs require very large data rates (e.g., tens of Gbps), and extremely good performance (low error probability) to be practical. In order to support the use of WiNoCs, communication link design must be done for these short-range networks in frequency bands above 100 GHz. A key part of the link design is design of the antennas and characterization of the resulting wireless channel. In this paper we explore such a design using a discone antenna. We show that relatively low-loss links that can support reliable 10 Gbps WiNoC data rates are attainable.

articleTitle: Optimization of the VSWR of reconfigurable antennas with a coupled multielement concept
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this contribution, an original reconfigurable antenna is proposed to offer an attractive tradeoff in terms of performances, complexity and cost. The originality consists in a panel with identical and periodical radiating elements. A reduced feed distribution network is associated to RF chains. Most elements are fed by couplings and associated to reflection-type phase shifters (RTPS). As a result, the size of the radiating aperture is maintained and the coupled elements are used as degrees of freedom to optimize the overall performances, and especially the active matching of the antenna. A 7×7 lattice of stacked patch antennas working at 5GHz has been investigated. The results obtained with this solution are presented and compared to an equivalent array using the same lattice.

articleTitle: Compact printed log-periodic dipole arrays fed by SIW horn
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) horn is a good planar feeding structure for planar antennas and arrays. In this letter, a 18 printed log-periodic dipole array (LPDA) antenna fed by a compact SIW horn is presented. Some linear arrays of metal vias are embedded inside the SIW horn to correct the phase and amplitude distributions on the horn aperture. The measured gain of the proposed antenna is 9.61 dBi, the half power beam-width is 18.1, the FTBR is 17.55 dB, the cross polarization in the axis direction is 21.48 dB, and the side-lobe lever is −14.93 dB at 10 GHz. Good agreement between the simulated and the measured results is obtained.

articleTitle: Design of a compact and low-profile wearable MIMO antenna for wireless personal area networks
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel wearable multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna using a circular high-impedance surface (HIS) is proposed in this paper for wireless personal area networks (WPANs). The antenna can operate from 2.4 to 2.49 GHz with a good port-to-port isolation (>15 dB). A pair of degenerated characteristic modes of a circular loop antenna are utilized to design the MIMO antenna, which makes the antenna much more compact than other artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) based MIMO antennas developed by using two independent antenna elements. To validate the proposed approach, a prototype was fabricated and measured. Measurements agree well with simulations. The antenna has a robust antenna performance against the human tissue and a low peak 1-g averaged SAR (0.55 W/kg) can be also observed. Meanwhile, its low-profile and compact geometry enables it to be a good candidate for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Surface mounted notch element for AESA applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A new surface mounted broadband notch element for AESA applications is presented. The radiating element is based on a traditional metal notch element but adapted for easy surface mounting by moving the feed point to the bottom of the element. A 7×7 element demonstrator array was designed, build and measured. Measured active reflection coefficient and radiation patterns are presented.

articleTitle: Dosimetric comparison using the human models reconstructed by precise segmentation, tissue simplification and template based registration
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Anatomical models are important in evaluating the human exposure to electromagnetic field. However, developing the anatomical model is very time- and labor — consuming. In the paper, we proposed two kinds of methods to reconstruct the individualized human model with high efficiency, which were based on the tissue simplification and the template based registration. The torso template was constructed with computerized tomography (CT) images of 79 healthy Chinese subjects. The numerical studies demonstrated that the model generated by template based registration had very few difference in terms of whole body averaged specific absorption rate and the power absorption in the major tissue layers, compared with the precisely segmented model.

articleTitle: New propagation regimes of symmetric hybrid waves in a nonlinear metal-dielectric waveguide
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The propagation of monochromatic nonlinear symmetric hybrid waves in a cylindrical nonlinear metal-dielectric waveguide is considered. The physical setting is reduced to a transmission eigenvalue problem for a system of ordinary differential equations which is new type of nonlinear eigenvalue problem where spectral parameters are the wave propagation constants. For the numerical solution, a method is proposed based on solving an auxiliary Cauchy problem (a version of the shooting method). As a result of comprehensive numerical modeling, new propagation regimes are discovered.

articleTitle: Broad-band efficient linearly polarization conversion ratio (PCR) metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this article, a wideband polarization conversion metasurfaces composed of frequency selective surface (FSS) is proposed. The simulation results indicate that polarization conversion ratio (PCR) is greater than 90% for both x- and y-polarization normally incident electromagnetic (EM) waves and the fractional bandwidth is approximately 96%. In addition, the metasurface is robust under broad-range incident oblique angles. The FSS metasurface processes the merit of wide bandwidth and efficient PCR, which demonstrates a promising future in modern communication systems and new polarization-control devices.

articleTitle: An improved directional modulation technique based on four-dimensional retrodirective arrays
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Four-dimensional (4-D) antenna arrays have been proved to be potential in physical layer secure communication. While in this work, the optimized time sequence can improve the feasibility of secrecy greatly. By introducing retro-directive technique into four-dimensional antenna array, the performance of secure communication can be realized without prior knowledge of the legitimate receiver's location, and avoid the heavy computation and complex hardware implementation. This is owing to the inherent advantages of retro-directive array in automatic target tracking. Moreover, the proposed transmitter architecture of 4-D retro-directive arrays are beneficial for the scenario of multiple legitimate receivers as well as the multipath environment.

articleTitle: Translational research into metasurface-based antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The latest progress in the metasurface-based antennas in the team from National University of Singapore is updated. As the two-dimensional version of the metamaterials also featuring unique electromagnetic properties, the metasurfaces have been the good candidates for the control of electromagnetic waves, in particular, antenna engineering. With the engineered electromagnetic properties of metasurfaces, we have developed the ultra-thin profile broadband dipole antennas for cellular base stations, low-profile broadband patch-type antennas for WiFi and millimeter-wave systems, the compact array with the suppression of high-order modes as well as the planar version of high-gain microwave lens antennas for beam-forming and multi-beam applications. Our research, development and commercialization (R&D&C) of metasurfaces in antenna engineering, we have shown the potential of translational research of new metasurafces in electromagnetic engineering.

articleTitle: Tackling hypertension via adrenal ablation — the development of novel immunohistochemical ablation biomarkers
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Microwave thermal ablation is under consideration for minimally invasive treatment of unilateral and bilateral adrenal adenomas, symptomatic of Conn's syndrome. Currently available microwave technologies are illsuited to precise ablation of small adrenal targets. In this study we report on the use of immunohistochemical markers as accurate microscopic markers of ablation damage extent. This ex vivo study will aid in efforts towards the design of microwave ablation systems for targeting adrenal masses. Microwave ablation was carried out on ex vivo bovine adrenal glands using various power outputs and ablation durations. The area of damage was assessed using histopathological, immunohistochemical and densitometry techniques. The immunohistochemical analysis illustrated the feasibility of this technique to microscopically detect the area of cell damage in tissue accurately. These results will aid in further investigation and development of microwave technology for precise ablation of adrenal masses.

articleTitle: A compact substrate integrated waveguide cavity backed antenna with stable radiation patterns for dual-band applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A compact dual-band cavity backed antenna with stable radiation pattern is proposed using substrate integrated waveguide technology. To make the dual-band operation, two radial cavities with different diameter are used to provide two desired frequency bands. The antenna is fed by a coaxial cable at its back and in line with the structure. This feed configuration makes the antenna compact. The satisfactory simulation and measurement results show that this antenna can be used in many dual-band applications.

articleTitle: A low-complexity array of directly phase modulating antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Direct antenna modulation (DAM), a radio transmitter technique where the RF carrier is modulated at the antenna, can allow low-complexity implementation of antenna arrays. Here, an antenna loaded with reconfigurable frequency selective surfaces (FSS) is designed to produce quadrature phase shift keying modulation (QPSK) and then simulated in a 2×2 array, where an amplified carrier is provided to each antenna by a simple feed network. The FSS is based on an aperture geometry loaded with varactor diodes where the phase and amplitude of the transmitted signal can be controlled with a bias voltage. Numerical simulations show that neighbouring antenna elements were found to cause a 9.2% variation in symbol magnitude and a 1.2° variation in symbol phase.

articleTitle: Novel ridge gap waveguide configuration supporting TEM propagation with lower loss and better isolation
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel ridge gap waveguide (RGW) configuration is presented. Its performance in terms of insertion loss and isolation is compared with the conventional structure made by periodic metallic pins. The structure is like an imaged RGW, but with half gap height. Therefore, it is symmetry unlike the conventional structure; the propagating mode is more like the TEM mode of the parallel plate waveguide, which we refer to as TEM-RGW. Compared to the conventional RGW with the same gap, the fringing fields are more confined to the ridge edges. Thus, it has a lower insertion loss and higher isolation.

articleTitle: Bulk ferroelectric materials for reconfigurable antenna applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Reconfigurable antennas are quickly becoming a requirement in modern communication systems that operate at multiple frequency bands, or have strict requirements for radiation pattern control. Ferroelectric materials have the unique property of an electric-field dependent relative permittivity, and can thus provide a novel way to control an radiating properties of antennas. In this paper, the latest developments and requirements of tunable microwave materials are discussed, and the way that they influence antenna design is highlighted. We present the measured tunability results of two different ferroelectric material compositions, barium strontium titanate and lead magnesium niobate — lead titanate, and discuss their suitability in antenna applications.

articleTitle: Optimization of the quad-ridged horn for the geodetic VGOS station of the Yebes observatory
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The next generation Very Long Baseline Interferometry (VLBI) radio telescope sited at the Yebes Observatory is a fully operative 13.2 m ring-focus reflector covering the frequency range from 2 to 14 GHz. A quad-ridged flared horn (QRFH) feed is one of the key components of the receiver system. Calibration methods using well-known celestial sources allow determining the aperture efficiency of the parabola, which in turn can be used as figure of merit for the design of the feed. Currently, the system provides efficiencies slightly above 50 %. With the aim of further improving its performance, a genetic algorithm, combining both physical optics and electromagnetic simulations, has been developed for the optimization of the QRFH feed. Preliminary results demonstrate the validity of the method.

articleTitle: Compact L/S-band circularly polarized microstrip antenna over reactive impedance surface
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A compact L/S-band circularly polarized (CP) antenna over the reactive impedance surface (RIS) is designed, fabricated, and measured. This dual-band CP antenna is excited by two probes and fed by two grounded coplanar waveguides. The CP radiation with very compact antenna size is achieved by stacking a square ring slotted truncated corner square patch and a truncated corner square patch over the RIS. The measured results show that the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of the antenna is 0.9% (1.787-1.803 GHz) for the lower band and 1.1% (2.6852.715 GHz) for the upper band, while the 10-dB return loss bandwidth is 5.9% (1.746-1.852 GHz) and 7.3% (2.586-2.784 GHz), respectively. The antenna gain at boresight is 1.9 dBic for the lower band, and 1.94 dBic for the upper band. The overall volume of the dual-band CP antenna is 0.235 × 0.235 × 0.042λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at 1.765 GHz.

articleTitle: Broadband mm-wave OFDM communications in doubly selective channel: Performance evaluation using measured mm-wave channel
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this work, we evaluate the performance of the broadband millimeter-wave (mm-wave) OFDM system in the presence of phase noise (PN) of phase-locked loop based oscillator and delay spread of measured mm-wave channel. It is shown, using Akaike's information criterion, that the channel tap coefficients of the broadband mm-wave channel do not follow Gaussian distribution due to the broad bandwidth. It is also shown that, given a cyclic prefix (CP) length for a certain delay spread, an effective PN mitigation scheme enables a PN corrupted OFDM system to function with small subcarrier spacing and, therefore, small CP overhead, with only slight degradation of the error rate performance.

articleTitle: A parallel channel sounder for MM wave channel measurement and modeling
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: To solve the difficulty of measuring the propagation characteristic of millimeter-wave band MIMO signal channel, this paper offers a parallel channel sounder with modular instruments for millimeter-wave band. It describes the difficulties of the design and development, the solutions and test experiments of the channel sounder. The post data processing result prove the validity of the proposed design of the sounder

articleTitle: Elevation angle dependence of building entry loss
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper a measurement campaign leading to a measurement model is presented. The channel sounding measurement campaign is performed to evaluate the effect of angle of elevation on building entry loss. It is reported in the paper that the losses due to angle of elevation can be upto 31 dB. The loss is shown to be linearly dependent on the angle of elevation. The proposed model is accepted as part of building entry loss in ITU-R recommendation.

articleTitle: A pattern reconfigurable microstrip antenna for future automotive applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a pattern reconfigurable patch antenna using parasitic elements and novel feeding method. The proposed antenna consist of a center-shorted microstrip patch antenna and two parasitic elements in its vicinity. Pattern reconfiguration is obtained by changing the length of parasitic elements using p-i-n diodes. Thanks to center-shorting, antenna size is reduced by about 50 %. The antenna can generate 3 reconfigurable patterns with a maximal gain of 9.5 dBi. Moreover, a multiple antenna system consisting of these antennas is proposed and evaluated. As a proof of concept a prototype of this antenna has been fabricated and measured. The maximal gain achieved is higher than 7.6 dBi. The measurement results correspond well with the simulation results in terms of S-parameter and radiation pattern.

articleTitle: Broadband linear polarization conversion metasurface based on grounded vias
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: An anisotropic high-impedance surfaces is applied to achieve perfect polarization rotation. Three multiple resonances are generated by electric and magnetic resonances which contributed to bandwidth expansion of the proposed polarization converter. The simulation results showed that maximum conversion efficiency is nearly 100% at mentioned three resonance frequencies. Here, 107 % bandwidth with polarization conversion ratio of above 90% is achieved. The proposed polarization conversion unit-cell is examined for oblique incidence, as well. It is observed that the bandwidth of the proposed unit-cell is not sensitive to the non-orthogonal incidence angles up to 40°. This observation verifies applicability of proposed polarization rotator unit-cell.

articleTitle: A novel single layer dual linear polarization band-pass frequency selective surface for automotive fully coated glass
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A single layer dual linear polarization Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) for automotive fully coated glass is presented. It acts as a band-pass filter for signals in the range of 640MHz to 3.3GHz. The performance of the proposed FSS element is assessed using CST Microwave Studio®. Simulations show less than 10dB of attenuation all over the frequency band for an angle of incidence up to 70° in both polarizations. This promising result makes from the proposed FSS a good candidate to overcome the problem of connectivity of a handled device inside the vehicle to the mobile network.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable multi-band antenna for miniature tracking terminal
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a miniature reconfigurable Inverted-F antenna (IFA) covering three different frequency bands. The target application is the Internet of Things (IoT) which requires the use of a miniature antenna to obtain location information using the GPS standard and send it to the server using the Low Power Wide Area Network (LP-WAN) standard.

articleTitle: Propagation prediction based on time domain electric field integral equation for smoothly irregular terrains
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a formulation to predict the propagation of a vertically polarized electromagnetic wave in the time domain using the Electric Field Integral Equation over an irregular terrain for a near grazing incidence. The results show good agreement when compared with the ones obtained from the Magnetic Field Integral Equation and the Uniform Theory of Diffraction, both in the time domain.

articleTitle: 360-degree polarization scanning with the diversity of boresight and conical patterns switching
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel reconfigurable antenna with the capability of 360-degree polarization scanning and the diversity of boresight and conical radiation patterns switching is presented in this paper. Each shorting-post is connected and controlled by a PIN diode to achieve the desired distribution of electric field null(s) in the substrate, where transverse magnetic (TM) modes switching between TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> can be accordingly realized corresponding to boresight and conical patterns. The antenna is analyzed in a cavity model, which, in terms of electric field, theoretically explains the generation of TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> and TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">02</inf> resonant modes, and provides the audience with an innovative method of designing pattern reconfigurable antennas for the applications such as multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO), wireless body sensor network (WBSN), Wi-Fi and WiMAX. The proposed antenna is with a competitive radius of 0.32 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>. The antenna structure is very easy to be fabricated. The measurement shows that the antenna can realize a boresight and conical pattern reconfiguration at 2.4 GHz with a gain of 6 dBi and efficiency of 86.7% (boresight mode), and 4.39 dBi and efficiency of 82.4% (conical mode).

articleTitle: Design of a wideband array antenna prototype with gap waveguide for w-band wireless links
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband 45° slot array antenna for W-Band wireless links. The proposed antenna prototype consists of 4 × 4 slot array, a wideband T-junction based on a groove gap waveguide and a vertical transition from WR-10 to groove gap waveguide. The simulated results show that the proposed prototype has an impedance bandwidth of 26.5% with input reflection coefficient better than −10 dB.

articleTitle: Efficient techniques for characteristic mode analysis of complex structures
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Characteristic mode analysis is an eigen analysis technique that is used to gain insight into the radiating properties of arbitrary electromagnetic structures. Real orthogonal current modes are obtained by solving a generalized symmetric eigenvalue problem defined by the real and imaginary parts of the Method-of-Moments impedance matrix. This work reviews the need for numerically efficient implementations of the calculation and post processing of characteristic modes.

articleTitle: Integrated beam-scanning antenna for heterodyne instruments at submillimeter-wave frequencies for martian climatology measurements
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present an integrated beam-scanning antenna for a submillimeter wave instrument. The ultimate goal is to be able to scan the limb of the Martian surface to measure the wind, temperature and water vapor. The scanning of the limb can be achieved by the mechanical translation of a micro-lens using a piezo-electric motor integrated with the receiver. A prototype has been fabricated and measured at 550 GHz, achieving a scanning loss lower than 0.4 dB for beam angles up to 15 degrees.

articleTitle: A sea-wave-dynamics monitoring radar based on propagation characteristics of echo signals
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: As human's marine activities, such as marine aquaculture, ocean shipping and coastal facilities construction, flourished world-widely, it is required to monitor the sea-wave dynamics timely and accurately. The radar introduced in this paper, namely "Sea-wave-dynamics Monitoring and Imaging System (SMIS)", working in the S-band at the center frequency of 3.1 GHz, is applicable to retrieving sea-wave dynamics. The SMIS emits a Quadrature-Phase-Shift-Keying (QPSK)-modulated sequence and receives the signal echoed by sea surfaces. The Channel Impulse Responses (CIRs) experienced by the received signals are calculated, and based on the CIRs, the so-called delay-concatenated maxpower Doppler frequency (DCMPD) spectrum is extracted. A simplified wave model is utilized to retrieve the sea-wave characteristics based on the analysis of the spatial-temporal periodic behavior of the DCMPD spectrum. The SMIS can be used to estimate the three-dimensional wave status, including the wave-height, wave-speed and wave-separation. Experimental valuation of the SMIS' performance has been conducted and the results demonstrate that the estimated sea-wave characteristics are consistent with those observed through a conventional buoy-based monitoring system.

articleTitle: 3D hodograph of antenna local phase center
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The concept of a local phase center (LPhC) as a geometric feature of the phase front of the radiation field contains a significant amount of uncertainty. The report discusses methodological aspects and computational particularity of determining the LPhC location caused by that uncertainty. The LPhC coordinates depend on the observation direction. In general, if observation direction alters, the LPhC moves along the 3D surface, or in the two-dimensional situation, along the hodograph-curve. They both often have an intricate configuration. Using a circle antenna array of elements with cardioid patterns as an example, we compare three computational algorithms. The comparison has revealed that commonly used defining the LPhC as the center of the inphase curve curvature can lead to erroneous results that are inconsistent with the physical sense.

articleTitle: Liquid-crystal reconfigurable, lens-enhanced, millimeter-wave phased array
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This article describes a novel concept of low-profile, lens-enhanced, reconfigurable millimeter-wave phased array. The proposed phased array comprised of multiple reconfigurable lens-enhanced radiators, which increases the effective aperture of each radiator and significantly reduces overall complexity and overall height of phased array. By using electrostatic controllable liquid-crystal-loaded metamaterial lens, transmission phase of each subarray of unit cells across the aperture can be electronically tuned independently. The array can be fed in groups to allow flexible hybrid beam forming for multiple beams, or can be fed with coherent phase across the aperture to form a highly directive steerable beam. Use of multiple feeds with smaller sub-arrays of unit cells also significantly reduces overall array profile since focal distance from the lens is reduced proportionally with smaller lenses. The proposed architecture allows forming of a versatile, low profile, beam scanning phased array with comparably high aperture efficiency for the future 5G deployment and satellite communications applications.

articleTitle: A posteriori antenna surface rework: A simple technique to correlate distortions to pattern degradations
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Many satellite communication systems for commercial television and radio applications and government and defense applications employ high-capacity high-frequency gateway links. Operating frequencies can get up to 30 GHz and higher (Ka-band). Thanks to their simplicity, shaped single offset antenna reflectors are often the preferred solution in the telecom satellite industry. A standard problem for shaped reflector antennas is related to surface distortions given by manufacturing errors. The variation of the distance between the primary source and the points on the surface of the reflector with respect to the nominal design is translated in a difference in phase at each point, which is usually the cause of degradation of performance. Areas of the pattern with very high gain requirements and quite steep roll-off are even more affected by surface distortions, which can lead to large performance degradation, not acceptable to meet the quality of service objectives. In Ka-band this effect is even more pronounced because of the higher frequency and demanding requirements. A simple technique to identify the area of the reflector which is the main cause of the pattern degradation is explained and a mechanical solution to mitigate the degradation is presented.

articleTitle: MM-wave slot array antenna backed by AMC reflector for 5G smartwatch applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel mm-wave phased array antenna for 5G smartwatch applications is proposed. The proposed array antenna consists eight rectangular slot antenna elements that are feed by inverted L shaped feed line and AMC reflector with 3 × 13 unit cells. The proposed array is designed to have near hemi-spherical coverage along with the high gain. The antenna performances on the human tissue phantom are investigated. The proposed array has good S-parameter characteristics in the frequency band ranging from 27.9 GHz to 29.1 GHz and mutual-coupling between antenna elements is less than -10 dB. The proposed array antenna has near hemispherical beam coverage suitable for 5G smartwatch application.

articleTitle: Dielectric methodologies of coaxial sensors for measurement of biological tissues up to 100 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this study, we summarize the dielectric methodologies used to measure dielectric properties of biological samples using a coaxial sensor. The measurement methodologies with model approximations were compared with those based on the analytical formula of the full-wave Maxwell equation. Here, the measurement of a rabbit cornea was conducted as an example. Results of these measurements are essential for analyzing systematic errors in the dielectric methodologies.

articleTitle: Centimeter-wave path loss and beam combining gain analysis for Belo Horizonte and Manaus environments in Brazil
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a cm-Wave measurement-based analysis of the path loss and a comparison with the SUI propagation model and the M.2135 and P.1411 ITU-R recommendations. These models were previously applied to mm-Wave measurements in the USA and Japan and it is probably the first analysis when considering cm-Wave measurements in Brazil. The measurement campaign was performed in two distinct regions of Brazil, in two different frequencies: Belo Horizonte, in the southeast region (18 GHz measurements), and Manaus, in the north region (24 GHz measurements). In the Belo Horizonte campaign the M.2135 Suburban recommendation best fits to the measurements and it was obtained a Beam Combining Gain of 4.5 dB when using the 5 strongest components of two measurement points. In Manaus urban environment, the M.2135 Urban Modified recommendation best fits to the measurements and for the suburban case the best fit was obtained with the SUI-B. It was also obtained a Beam Combining Gain of 4 dB when using the 5 strongest components.

articleTitle: Prediction of tumor heatability in microwave hyperthermia applicators
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, the heating efficiency of two hyperthermia applicators has been evaluated for the treatment of tumors in the brain. The effect of a high number of antennas and lower frequencies were investigated by employing one applicator with many antennas and one applicator with antennas operational in a lower frequency range. An investigation method was first used to find out the most difficult and easy places for heating inside the head. Given the applicator, patient model, and tumor position, the method is assessing whether or not the applicators are able to heat the tumor efficiently.

articleTitle: Effect of line of sight in clustering distribution of signal contribution at 5.8 GHz indoor environments
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Indoor propagation at 5 GHz band is receiving new interest as 2.4 GHz band is becoming more and more saturated. In this contribution, we studied the clustering distribution generated in the delay domain, comparing both line of sight and non-line of sight conditions. The work is based on the results of a large broadband measurement campaign performed within an indoor environment. We also presented and described a comparison between both scenarios, providing insight on the behavior of such environments at 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: An eigenmode method with improved accuracy for guided waves
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A finite difference frequency domain eigenmode method with improved accuracy for guided waves is presented. The presented method takes the conducting edge field singularity into account.
