We also introduce an Analytic-Spline-Hybrid (ASH) optimization scheme for the QRFH ridge and sidewall profiles.

articleTitle: Design of a simultaneous X/Ka-band SATCOM-on-the-move terminal for commercial and military applications with monopulse tracking in both bands
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The design of a simultaneous X/Ka band SATCOM-on-the-Move (SOTM) terminal with monopulse tracking in both X-band and Ka-band is presented. The Ka-band of this terminal covers part of the Commercial Ka-band as well as the Military Ka-band.

articleTitle: Measurement based spatial characteristics of MPCs in train-to-train propagation
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Railway operators for high speed trains, commuter trains or subways request for technologies to increase the density and efficiency on their rails. One of those future technologies is virtual coupling based on train-to-train (T2T) wireless communication links. For the design of a wireless communication system, the knowledge of wave propagation is crucial. To characterize the propagation effects between two moving trains a T2T channel sounding measurement campaign was performed. To post-process the data, we use the Kalman enhanced super resolution tracking (KEST) algorithm to detect and track multipath components (MPCs). Using the single-input single-output measurement data recorded while the transmitter and receiver were in motion, the complex amplitude, the delay and the life time of individual MPCs can be estimated. First results of the post-processing step, the geometrical representation of MPCs using point scatterers and possibilities to identify scattering positions are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Characterization challenges for millimeter-wave multi-antenna 5G devices
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Millimeter-wave 5G UE (user equipment) devices are expected to incorporate multiple signaling antennas due to the potential for blockage by head, hand, and body. These new types of devices present new test challenges not present with today's sub-6 GHz UE devices. In particular, test methods currently agreed to by 3GPP assume no knowledge of the locations of the multiple antennas or even which antenna is active at a given time. Consequently, any far-field measurement must employ a quiet zone sufficiently large to encompass the entire device. For a typical 5G UE operating at 28 GHz and 15 cm along the longest diagonal dimension, the minimum far-field separation between the probe antenna and device is 4.2 m. In this paper, we will discuss and experimentally demonstrate the types of measurement errors anticipated for a multi-antenna UE device characterized with a far-field distance sufficient to test an individual antenna but insufficient to test antennas across the larger UE device. We also show experimental results obtained from a compact antenna test range (CATR) and confirm that it provides accurate measurements in a relatively smaller footprint than a traditional far-field measurement.

articleTitle: Large deployable antennas benchmark for contoured beam mission in C band
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We report an RF benchmark study of large deployable antennas for a contoured beam mission in C band. With conventional solid shaped reflector antennas being limited to diameters of 3 m, we investigate solid shaped reflector antennas with aperture diameters of 3 m and 6 m as well as 6 m mesh reflector and reflectarray antennas. We consider a European coverage with directivity and XPD goals, and a realistic corrugated horn feed in a single-offset reflector configuration for the design of solid, mesh and reflectarray antennas. Our study shows that several 6 m mesh and reflectarray antennas perform better than the 3 m solid shaped antenna, which, upon further technological maturation, may pave the way for one or more of these novel antenna concepts in future contoured beam applications, when large (>3 m) apertures are required.

articleTitle: Closed-to-open conversion of a mm-wave Gaussian horn antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents an application of the powerful field modal expansion theory, to derive a mm-wave "open" cross-section gaussian horn antenna starting from a standard closed cross section design. The proposed approach is based on the expansion of the open-structure field in the orthonormal basis of the closed structure. The calculation of an inner product between the closed- and open-structures electromagnetic modes allows to mathematically evaluate and control the "distance" between the original closed and the derived open structure. The proposed methodology has been successfully tested by comparing FDTD simulation results between the closed and the open mm-wave TEn-Guassian converter.

articleTitle: Compact 3D-printed variable-infill antenna for snow cover monitoring
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The negative effects of snow avalanches can be highly reduced by risk mitigation strategies, such as villages evacuation or closure of road. Avalanche forecasting is crucial for improving the effectiveness of such strategies, and it largely depends on the capability of monitoring the internal properties of the snow cover. While manual analysis of the snow cover still remains the most used technique, very accurate but time consuming and with several limitations on the safety side, microwave radar systems have demonstrated being a viable solution for non-manual snow monitoring, with enormous benefits in terms of measurement speed and safety. A key component for such radars is the antenna, which is required to exhibit large bandwidths, to achieve accurate resolutions, reasonable gain and input matching, to do not impair the system sensitivity, and to be as compact and light as possible, to be compatible with portable devices and on-the-move installations. This paper presents the design, simulation results and fabrication proposal of a 3D-printed double-ridge waveguide antenna specifically studied for snow monitoring. The proposed antenna weights around 100 g, with an encumbrance in the order of 5.16 × 2.40 × 6.78 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, while maintaining a working bandwidth from 2.25 GHz to 5.8 GHz.

articleTitle: The new large antenna positioning system for over-the-air testing at the National Institute of Standards and Technology
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper introduces the new Large Antenna Positioning System (LAPS) at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). For the last eight years NIST has been pioneering the use of robotics for antenna measurements. Starting with the development and integration of the Configurable Robotic Millimeter-Wave Antenna (CROMMA) facility. CROMMA was designed to be reconfigurable to different near-field antenna measurement geometries and perform antenna measurements from 100 to 500 GHz. Probe position repeatability of 25 μm was achieved using coordinate metrology feedback. However, the single-robotic-armed CROMMA was restricted to small antennas. To overcome this limitation, NIST developed the concept of a dual-robot system with one fixed and the other mounted on a large linear rail slide. Using characterization of the robotic arm joints and segments, the LAPS will have open loop probe position accuracies of 200 μm to facilitate antenna measurements up to 30 GHz.

articleTitle: Impact of capacitive coupling element design on antenna bandwidth
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A coupling element is typically used to excite one of more characteristic modes of a structure to form some desired radiation properties. In particular, non-resonant coupling elements (CEs) are attractive, since it is electrically small and can be more conveniently integrated into the structure, such as the chassis of a mobile terminal. In this case the chassis is the primary radiator of the mobile terminal. However, there is still limited knowledge on how to design and optimize coupling elements. In this paper, we examine how the dimensions of a single capacitive coupling element (CCE) influence the potential bandwidth of exciting the fundamental dipole mode of a rectangular terminal chassis. The parametric study shows that the CCE must not be too small electrically, for the sake of bandwidth. However, the bandwidth saturates when the size of the CCE is increased beyond a certain threshold. Therefore, this study provides some useful insights and guidelines for CCE design.

articleTitle: A modular phased array transceiver with RF-MEMS SPDT switches in a 0.25 μm SiGe BiCMOS technology
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: An highly-integrated active reflectarray transceiver enhanced with fully monolithically integrated RF-MEMS SPDT switches is presented. The system operates at Ka band and follows a 3-D manifold concept incorporating wide angle scanning antenna elements, RF interconnects, mixed-signal MMICs in a flexible and scalable manner. Apart from this, the thermal management of the system, as well as the robustness and reliability of RF-MEMS SPDT switches are discussed. To verify the technological methodology, a phased array demonstrator with 144 elements has been realized demonstrating excellent scanning performance up to 60° from boresight.

articleTitle: Performance testing of massive MIMO base station with multi-probe anechoic chamber setups
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The utilization of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna arrays at the base station (BS) side has been identified as an enabling technique for 5G communication systems. To evaluate the true end-to-end performance of BS's, an over-the-air (OTA) radiated method is required. In this paper, we present a sectorized multi-probe anechoic chamber (MPAC) configuration equipped with a switch box for massive MIMO BS OTA testing. Simulations were performed for a BS equipped with an 8 × 8 planar array of half-wavelength element spacing at 3.5 GHz, where 1 m measurement range and 8 active OTA probes are considered. Due to the important role of beamforming techniques in 5G antenna arrays, the Bartlett beamforming power patterns under the channel models reproduced in the MPAC setups are utilized to quantify the channel emulation accuracy.

articleTitle: Semidefinite relaxation-based optimization of Yagi-Uda array antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The semidefinite relaxation-based optimization framework developed for finding the physical limits on the performance of WPT systems is adopted for optimization of antenna array gain in the far-field. The technique is adapted to account for typical antenna design requirements by adding power constraints for impedance matching considerations. Simulation examples and comparisons to global optimization verify the applicability, versatility and reliability of this powerful and general method in the context of Yagi-Uda array antennas.

articleTitle: Comparative channel study of ray tracing and measurement for an indoor scenario at 28 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The millimeter wave communication is important for future wireless systems. In this paper, the channel characteristics at 28 GHz in an indoor scenario are researched based on ray tracing (RT) simulation and measurement. In the RT simulation, various configurations, such as different number of reflections, diffractions and penetrations are used. As for the measurement, two setups are implemented in order to analyze more parameters. Setup one is that biconical antennas are used at both the transmitter (TX) and receiver (RX). The other setup is that horn antenna at RX is rotated 360° in azimuth with a step of 5° when an omni-directional antenna located at TX. Meanwhile, antenna is rotated one circle with an elevation angle of 10°, 0° and −10°, respectively. Path loss and K-factor are analyzed firstly, and analysis results indicate the RT result with 1 or 2 reflections, 1 diffractions and 5 penetrations in this conference room is closest to the measurement result and channel models in 3GPP TR 38.901. Then, the root mean square (RMS) delay spread and RMS angular spread are investigated, which shows the value of measurement is a bit larger than RT because of the limitation of azimuth and elevation step. According to all the results, 1–2 reflections, 1 diffraction and 5 penetrations can be used in RT for future analysis of indoor scenario at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Robust and compact PDMS antennas for search and rescue operations and emergency communications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Wearable antennas are a topic of interest in the RF and microwave community. Over the last two decades many studies have been conducted which have led to the development of several devices that are now used in many sectors such as healthcare, military and athletics. In this paper, a folded-shorted patch (FSP) compact antenna and a circular polarized (CP) patch antenna were developed and are operational at about 400 MHz and 2.45 GHz, respectively. Polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) is used as the substrate for both the antennas in order to make them resilient to different environments, be low profile and wearable. These antennas can be useful for search and rescue operations and emergency services as they can provide compactness and flexibility of movement while maintaining antenna radiation performances. To prove durability and resiliency of the fabricated antennas, robustness tests such as bending, wet and temperature tests were performed for the CP patch. Additionally, the realized gain pattern was measured when the CP patch antenna was placed inside a ballistics jacket with experimental results demonstrating antenna operation.

articleTitle: Exploiting the orthogonality sampling method to design virtual scattering experiments
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The orthogonality sampling method is a recently introduced qualitative method for imaging the location and shape of objects embedded in unknown scenario from the knowledge of their scattered fields. As compared to other qualitative methods, orthogonality sampling is remarkably simpler, as it does not involve the choice of regularization parameters and can be applied also for single incidence. In this contribution, we investigate the possibility of using the method as a new tool to condition the scattering phenomenon and to design virtual scattering experiments. As a matter of fact, the unique features of the orthogonality sampling method could open the way to new and more generally applicable inversion methods based on the virtual experiment framework.

articleTitle: Results of medium wave HD radio mobile reception measurements in a dense urban region
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This document presents the results of the statistical analysis of digital radio mobile measurements performed in a dense urban region of Brazil. Measurements at medium wave were carried out in São Paulo using an HD Radio standard transmitter. The path loss exponent was estimated for each measurements route, as well as the large-scale and small-scale fading cumulative probability distribution functions for the received signals. Also, the results presented here include coverage and reception quality in mobility conditions.

articleTitle: Systematic octopus-shape antenna design with circular polarization by characteristic mode theory
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Characteristic Mode Theory (CMT) is used to design patch antennas with nature-inspired shapes to show the high performance of this theory in designing of circularly polarized antennas. Furthermore, the suerformula is devised to generate various planar geometries existing in nature, such as corolla and petals. Two antennas are designed to demonstrate the capability of combination of CMT and superformula to provide a physical insight in the antenna radiation and also realizing novel antenna patch geometries. The first antenna has circular polarization at 2.45 GHz, which is excited by a single probe feed. The second antenna is dual band, which is designed for circular polarization in the first band and also the second band is controlled by the application of CMT. The antennas are designed for the ISM band which have commercial applications.

articleTitle: A compact low-cost direction finding system for unmanned aerial vehicles
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper considers the application where a small unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) must determine the bearing to another UAV already in flight in an environment where GPS is denied through malicious jamming. The development therefore presents the design of a compact and low-power circuit architecture for radio frequency direction finding. The system uses switches to sequentially connect the elements of a circular array antenna to the receive circuitry. While simple architecturally, this causes phase differences between estimates that must be calibrated through use of a reference receive channel. A MUSIC-based bearing estimator developed on a small on-board processor shows the ability to accurately estimate the azimuth and elevation angles to the remote UAV during experimental flight tests.

articleTitle: Realization of FDA using variable-period time modulated technique
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Frequency diverse array (FDA) is attractive because of its range-dependent beampattern. However, the realization of FDA is very complex and expensive in hardware. In this paper, a simple method is proposed to realize FDA based on variable-period time modulated technique (VPTMT). Each antenna element is followed by a I/Q channel modulator which is composed of power dividers, switches and phase shifters. The frequency offset and the corresponding phase shift can be achieved by adjusting the modulate period and the switch-on time instants of the switchers, respectively. Both of them can be controlled by FPGA control board easily, and no extra frequency source is needed. To show the effectiveness of the proposed method, some simulation results are provided.

articleTitle: Impact of adverse weather conditions on multi-layer radomes installed in arctic regions
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The impact of adverse weather conditions on the satellite communication can entail a significant deterioration of the link between the Ground Station (GS) and the satellite. The effects are in addition emphasized at higher frequencies (i.e. K-band), where the atmospheric losses are greater respect to the lower frequencies. The use of Radomes, opportunely designed for the specific applications, to cover and protect the GSs is essential to guarantee the operations. However, a wet Radome caused by rainy conditions may introduce a strong signal attenuation, and therefore during the preliminary phase it is necessary to know how this inconvenience influences the performance of the system. In this paper a prediction model, useful to estimate the performance of a Multi-Layer (MLR) Radome under adverse weather condition, is presented. In addition, an experimental characterization of hydrophobic materials is addressed.

articleTitle: Design of a metasurface covered slotted waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Slotted waveguides antennas can benefit from the use of a metasurface cover, so that the E-Plane cut of the radiation pattern narrows and the directivity increases. Based on this principle, this paper discusses the design of a metasurface covered slotted waveguide antenna. The impact of the metasurface on the slot properties is analyzed. Finally an example of a Taylor distribution design is given, showing the improvements in gain.

articleTitle: Linear LINC transmitters using dual-polarized power-combining antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: It is common practice to use nonlinear, high-efficient power amplifiers to transmit non-constant envelope signals using concepts like LINC (linear amplification using nonlinear components). Traditional systems use a power combiner to reconstruct the non-constant envelope RF signal that is fed into the antenna. In this paper, we will investigate the integration of the power combiner with the radiator, resulting in a LINC power-combining antenna concept. Our novel concept uses two polarizations where the full reconstruction of the signal is done at the receiver side. System-level measurements at 2.45 GHz with 32-QAM signals show that our power-combining antenna concept out-performs traditional LINC implementations.

articleTitle: Measurement-based massive MIMO channel characterization in subway station
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, measurements of massive multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) radio channel are conducted in subway station scenarios. The measurements are conducted at the center frequency of 6 GHz with a bandwidth of 100 MHz. A virtual 64 × 4 planar antenna array is used at the transmitter (Tx), and a single antenna is placed at 34 different locations as the receiver (Rx). The typical channel characteristics are extracted, including channel gain, root mean square delay spread (RMS-DS), and K-factor. These results indicate that the spatial variations occur across the two-dimension (2D) large-scale antenna array. The variations are further investigated by modeling these features with respect to the distance between the Tx and the Rx. The results are useful for characterizing the non-stationary massive MIMO channels.

articleTitle: 3D-printed mm-wave corrugated plate antenna for 5G communications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A design of novel 3D printed antenna for millimeter-wave and 5G applications is presented in this paper. The proposed 3D printed antenna consists of 3D printed radiating structure and a feeding layer. Moreover, the proposed antenna is compact and small and it has been fabricated using simple and low cost method. The proposed antenna is fabricated using 3D-printing and novel metallization technique, where the 3D-printed prototype is metalized using conductive spray-coating technology which is traditionally used for EMI/RFI Shielding applications. The proposed antenna resonates at 28.5 GHz with a measured −10 dB bandwidth of 3.5 GHz. In addition, it has a simulated peak gain 9.6 dBi and an average gain of higher than 9 dBi over most of its bandwidth.

articleTitle: Vehicle-to-vehicle channel characteristics in municipal lake scenarios at 5.9 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper focuses on vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) radio channel characteristics based on measurements at 5.9 GHz under urban-lake-urban (ULU) and urban-lake-suburb (ULS) scenarios. Power delay profile (PDP), propagation path loss, and delay spread are obtained from measurement data and described for each scenario. The comparison between ULU and ULS shows : the number of reflection path is significantly larger in the ULU scenario; the multipath signals number of ULU is about 7 paths higher than that in ULS on average, and the path loss in ULS is 2.12 dB higher than that in ULU; it is also found that the statistics of mean excess and RMS delay spread match lognormal distribution well; the mean excess delay and RMS delay spread of ULS are lower than that in ULU.

articleTitle: TCM-based miniaturization progress of a square microstrip patch antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A miniaturized square microstrip patch antenna (MPA) is analyzed and designed using the theory of characteristic mode (TCM). The TCM is applied to investigate and adjust the current distribution of the lowest resonance mode that the square patch can support. Based on the current distribution of the concerned mode, the two opposite edges of the patch where the characteristic current mainly concentrates on are curved with quadratic function curves. Then stubs are periodically loaded on the curved-edges, and the current along the curved-edges occurs slight changes. At last, two apertures are etched on the patch, and more current trends to flow along the edges of the apertures. The above three approaches are examined through TCM, and all lead to reduction of resonance frequency of concerned mode. After optimizing the position of the probe-fed, a 60% miniaturization in the size of the square MPA is achieved. The TCM is expected to provide more effective guidance in antenna miniaturization design.

articleTitle: Preliminary configuration design of mesh antennas using integrated structural-electromagnetic method
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: For mesh antennas, the lattice of their surface configuration is one of the most critical factors those affect the electromagnetic (EM) performance. Since using some traditional configuration design method will lead to faceted surface with periodic geometric approximation error that can result in strong grating lobes, and besides, the faceted surface configuration and the cable pretensions are interdependent, when designing the surface configuration of mesh antennas, both the EM performance and the structural factors should be taken into consideration. Therefore, in this paper, an integrated structural-electromagnetic configuration design method is proposed. The aim is to minimize the maximum grating lobe level with constrained gain, first side lobe level and cable pretensions. Numerical example results show that the proposed method can greatly decreased the grating lobe level without degrading the antenna gain or increasing the first side lobe level with specified cable tensions.

articleTitle: Waveform matching based real-time ablation monitoring for microwave breast cancer ablation
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: As a minimal invasive tool for cancer treatment, microwave ablation (MWA) is promising. For safety and effective ablation for cancerous tissue, the real-time monitoring for the dimensions of the ablation zone should be implemented. This study focuses on microwave based MWA monitoring. The time difference of arrival (TDOA) based imaging algorithm is one of most promising methods, which achieves real-time, and highly noise-robust imaging using a prior knowledge of only dielectric constants of tissues surrounding probe, pre and during ablation states. However, it often suffers from an inaccuracy for imaging, especially in the lower impact of the ablation. To enhance the accuracy, this paper proposes the waveform matching based algorithm, where the impact of conductivity drop is also considered in boundary estimation. The statistical test with 100 different ablation cases, using the finite difference time domain (FDTD) simulation, using realistic breast phantoms derived from MRI, demonstrate that the proposed method offers more accurate ablation zone imaging, compared with that obtained by the TDOA based method, maintaining a real-time property.

articleTitle: Four dimensional antenna arrays for wideband transmit beamforming
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This work presents a study on the application of wideband transmit beamforming by four-dimensional (4D) linear antenna arrays. Other than existing technologies of 4D antenna arrays that only focus on narrow band applications, the transmission of wideband signal is firstly considered. Wideband linear frequency modulation (LFM) pulse is used as the input of 4D antenna arrays and the waveforms after the time modulation are analyzed. Wideband beam patterns, which represent the relationship among radiation power, emission angle and frequency, are calculated. Then, numerical results using different time sequences are given to confirm that 4D antenna arrays can be applied to wideband signal transmission.

articleTitle: Electronically switchable notch response for wideband bandpass applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a wideband bandpass filter with a switchable notch response in a single device. The bandpass filter is designed using 7th order short circuited stub filter. Then, the first short circuited stub is replaced with two sections of open circuited stub to exhibit the transmission zeros at lower/higher stopband. Then, this type of filter is combined with a U-shaped SIR and PIN diode to realize a switchable notch response of 5.2 GHz. The fabricated result shows good agreement with the simulated results. This type of filter is very useful for any wireless and radar applications.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized fabry-perot antenna fed by an arbitrarily-rotated source
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This work proposes a novel circularly-polarized Fabry-Perot antenna. The rotation of the feeding source is used as an additional degree of freedom to establish a circular polarized radiation. The design of the antenna resorts to an accurate tool based on a spectral Green's function approach. The design of an ideal circularly-polarized structure is thus proposed and validated by full-wave simulations.

articleTitle: High gain K-band patch antenna for low earth orbit interlink between nanosatellites
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband or high gain 4×4 array operating in k-band. The unit cell of this array is a rectangular patch antenna in a stacked configuration. Four rectangular patches are passively excited by an additional rectangular patch located underneath. The latter is excited by a substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) through an aperture etched on the ground plane. By moving the relative position, and therefore the overlapped area, between the passive patches and the active one, a wideband or a high gain behavior can be obtained, maintaining the same layout. The proposed array achieves the impedance bandwidth of 12.55% with a gain of 22 dBi for the wideband case. In the high gain case, the impedance bandwidth is 5.5% with a gain of 24 dBi.

articleTitle: A novel 1-bit reconfigurable element for wideband and multi-polarization reflectarray
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel wideband 1-bit element for reconfigurable linearly and circularly polarized reflectarray. The design is based on the capacitance-coupled patch antenna with four PIN diodes for the polarization and phase control of the reflected wave. Utilizing dual-polarization feeding techniques, the proposed element can receive the incidence wave in one polarization while reflect the wave in the other polarization. Such polarization-rotation feature makes the designed element can be used to achieve wideband and multi-polarization reflectarray antennas. The stable performance of the proposed element under oblique incidence is also observed.

articleTitle: Persistent Q anti-collision algorithm for RFID
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In passive Radio Frequency Identification Systems (RFIDs), the interrogator should energise clients within range and use their backscattered replies to identify an inventory as quickly as possible. However, at the interrogator replies from two or more energised clients may collide and collided clients may not be identified. Therefore, collisions increase the number of timeslots needed to record an inventory. Reducing the number and frequency of collisions is an important and topical area research in RFID. Previously for passive Ultra High Frequency RFID the problem of collisions has been addressed using an ALOHA based protocol called the Q-Selection Algorithm. In this paper, a more efficient algorithm is presented that is shown to reduce the number of timeslots needed to record an inventory by approximately 30% when compared to the existing Q algorithm.

articleTitle: Uncertainty quantification for reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Large reflector antennas for telecommunication or space observation purposes often require a lengthy and detailed design process, where the design is carefully revised to ensure the best performance for the intended application. For many modern reflector antennas, quantification of the uncertainty in performance as a function of manufacturing errors is an important part of the design process. In this paper, we present an efficient way of quantifying the effects of uncertainty in the production. The method is shown to far outperform the conventional MonteCarlo techniques in accuracy and computational time.

articleTitle: FDTD based simulation study of a classification based hemorrhagic stroke detector
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The possibility to detect intracranial bleedings caused by stroke or head trauma in a prehospital setting would be a major breakthrough in the strive to deliver the best possible care for these patients. Our research is focused on developing a microwave based diagnostic system for prehospital use, which is capable of detecting intracranial bleedings. This paper contains a numerical simulation study to investigate the detection capability of a machine learning algorithm and its performance for differentiating hemorrhagic stroke from patients with no bleeding. The goal is to assess the performance of the detection algorithm as a function of the number of patients included in the training phase. The results show that this approach is feasible, but that it requires one thousand patients for training the algorithm, in order to reach a detection rate with AUC values approaching 0.9.

articleTitle: Demonstration of superdirectivity for PCB split ring dimers
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We have designed and tested a Metamaterial Superdirective Antenna (MSA). The MSA was fabricated using PCB technique and comprised a pair of split ring resonators (SRRs). It achieved high directivity with a compact design which is easy to manufacture. Superdirectivity was predicted by simulations and verified by experimental results. The coupling between the SRR's was varied to maximize directivity. The potential for designing the MSA to any operating frequency was explored.

articleTitle: Hexaferrite substrate versus impedance matching for tuneable patch antenna miniaturisation
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Novel hexaferrite substrates and impedance matching networks are both means to deliver electrically small antennas (ESAs). The performance characteristics of each are often restricted to a discussion on the reflection coefficient S11, without consideration of full radiative characterisation. In this work the radiation efficiency and pattern of a hexaferrite patch ESA and impedance-matched sub-resonant Rogers RT5880 patch were compared. The efficiencies of each technique were found to be low, while the pattern of the sub-resonant patch displayed considerable divergence from the half-wavelength behaviour of the hexaferrite patch. The stability of the magnetically-tuned radiation pattern of the hexaferrite patch was then demonstrated over a tuned bandwidth of 32.1%.

articleTitle: Reflectarray synthesis on GPUs
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper the role of the GPU in the reflectarray synthesis is highlighted. In particular the details related to the implementation of the Non Uniform FFT routine, exploited to accelerate the pattern evaluation, and of a parallel Particle Swarm optimizer employed in the early stages of the synthesis are here reported.

articleTitle: Time-domain analysis of classical omnidirectional axis-displaced dual-reflector antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This work presents an approach to obtain the time-domain electric far field radiated by classical omnidirectional dual-reflector antennas fed by a TEM coaxial horn. The time-domain formulation is developed by means of analytical inversion of the corresponding frequency-domain solution obtained using Geometrical Optics (GO) principles and the aperture method.

articleTitle: A multi-carrier frequency diverse array design method for wireless power transmission
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The design and optimization of uniformly-excited and nonuniformly-excited frequency diverse arrays (FDAs) for far-field wireless power transmission (WPT) are addressed. A new optimization-based multi-carrier FDA design method using nonlinear frequency offsets and time-modulated weights is proposed, allowing the energy to be focused over a defined collection region with an optimal end-to-end energy transfer efficiency in the range-angle dimensions. Preliminary numerical results are reported and discussed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed multi-carrier WPT-FDA approach also in comparison with the state-of-the-art WPT design solutions.

articleTitle: Ultra high figure-of-merit mushroom nanoantenna array for refractive index sensing
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, we introduce a developed version of mushroom nanoantenna sensor array suitable for refractive index sensing. The single element structure consists of gold-silica disks placed on top of a silica film backed by a gold layer. The whole structure is supported by silicon substrate, which is a passive substrate shielded from electromagnetic fields. The presence of the ground plan allows for isolating the proposed sensor from the medium underneath, which make it immune against parasitic variations in the supporting medium. The proposed developed mushroom sensor is fully optimized using a rigorous optimization algorithm. It shows a figure-of-merit (FoM) as high as 579, which is significantly better than other versions of mushroom sensors already presented in literature. The proposed device is fabricated using Electron Beam Lithography (EBL).

articleTitle: Low-pass frequency selective surface for a dual-band gyro-multiplier characterized by THz-TDS
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This work investigates the performance of a low-pass frequency selective surface (FSS) fabricated from perforated hole array on a copper plate for the use in a dual-band high power gyro-multiplier. The output beam from the high power gyro-multiplier contains signals at two separating bands carrying peak power up to 2 kW. The frequency separating components therefore are required to stand high power and produce low insertion loss. Metallic perforated array is an ideal option to meet these requirements. Considering the fabrication accuracy, low-pass FSS is selected. The fabrication of the low-pass FSS is based on precision milling technology. The performance of the FSS is evaluated using a terahertz time domain spectroscopy.

articleTitle: Alphasat experiment in madrid: modeling considerations on fade and inter-fade duration results
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The Q-band Alphasat beacon signal is being received in Madrid and now three complete years of measurements are available (from March 2014 to February 2017). In previous works the characteristics of the experiment -such as experimental setup and data processing—and attenuation results have been presented. This paper presents fade and inter-fade results for the average year, a modeling process that includes a comparison against models and a fitting effort on fade and inter-fade distributions. From these, it is concluded that there is room for improvement for fade duration models and that inter-fade duration distributions can be well approximated with two lognormal distributions, for durations lower than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> s.

articleTitle: Influence of a metallic radiator on a multiband LTE MIMO antenna system
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the influence of a metallic radiator in the very close environment of a MIMO antenna system, with four accesses located at the four corners of the ground plane. Each access feeds a radiating structure made up of three radiating elements: a main folded monopole and two parasitic folded elements. This antenna designed to be placed in a smart cell to cover three LTE bands: [0.7–0.9], [1.71–1.88] and [2.5–2.69] GHz. While its presence could have penalized them, the performances of the antenna were improved with this radiator used as a reflector, allowing to reduce the back radiation, to reflect it forward and thus to double the realized gain (5.75 dB), therefore allowing to reduce the return loss, and to improve the efficiency (80%).

articleTitle: Multi-antenna configuration modeling for massive MIMO V2I
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: There is a growing research interest in massive Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) antenna systems because of their higher channel capacity and energy efficiency. New applications in digital mobility and connected car is certainly one of the areas of future development of these systems. In order to study the impact of the different multi-antenna geometries and MIMO modalities in both the vehicle and the fixed base station, a quality modeling of a realistic scenario is needed. In this paper, study of initial antenna configurations for both — mobile and fixed — platforms is performed and initial channel parameters and system capability are obtained. Then, several systems and constellations are compared by means of the channel eigenvalues and capacity. The analysis is based on the results of a simulated model of an urban scenario, emulating as a case of study a portion of the city of Barcelona in a realistic environment, comprising of a massive MIMO base station and a car at various positions.

articleTitle: Linear antenna transient analysis using running fourier transform and page spectrum
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This article deals with conception of applying the running energy density spectrum and Page transform in analyzing input current of linear antenna for short pulse excitation. This transformation works in the real numbers domain and do not generate cross terms which are disadvantage of other two-dimensional transformations. In our investigation we employ Page transformation in order to achieve the running spectrum of dipole transient response for Gaussian pulse excitation. Using running spectrum we were able to observe and visualize many features of considered processes.

articleTitle: Challenges for future active space communication array antennas
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, major challenges for electronically reconfigurable satellite communication antennas are discussed. Needs for future telecommunication missions, especially very high throughput geostationary satellite missions as well as low/medium earth orbit mission needs are considered. Future science missions of ESA are also discussed. Key challenges are illustrated by sample array antenna geometries for representative requirements.

articleTitle: Exploitation of frequency diversity in GPR imaging through an innovative constrained-BCS method
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This work deals with the retrieval of the electromagnetic (EM) properties of buried domains starting from wide-band ground penetrating radar (GPR) measurements. The GPR inverse scattering (IS) problem is formulated within the contrast source framework and solved through an innovative multi-task Bayesian compressive sensing (MT-BCS)-based approach. More precisely, the developed methodology integrates a customized MT-BCS solver inside a frequency-hopping (FH) inversion strategy. Thanks to a novel "constrained" relevance vector machine (C-RVM) algorithm, progressively acquired information about the solution through the cascaded processing of different frequency components can be effectively exploited. Some numerical results are shown in order to assess the effectiveness of the proposed FH-MT-BCS method, as well as to compare it against a single-task (FH-STBCS) implementation not exploiting the correlation among different illuminations.

articleTitle: Design of a benchtop RF vector parameter analyzer
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper proposed a novel benchtop RF vector parameter analyzer (VPA), integrating the functions of microwave vector signal generation and vector signal analysis, with flexible framework, unified RF subsystem, and efficient signal process algorithms, such as Newton backward interpolation algorithm for the arbitrary sample rate conversion. It can be conveniently applied in many cases such as RF modules and transceivers test, substituting for signal generator and analyzer, with a considerable lower cost.

articleTitle: New in-vivo estimation of electrical properties of biological tissues for hyperthermia treatment planning
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The estimation of conductivity and permittivity of biological tissues is fundamental in the determination of the specific absorption rate (SAR) and electromagnetic field intensity distribution in hyperthermia treatment planning. In this contribution, an original approach for the in-vivo estimation of these parameters is introduced. The proposed approach is based on the solution of an inverse scattering problem and the innovative use of the morphological map of biological tissue exacting by medical images, obtained by means of magnetic resonance imaging or computed tomography.

articleTitle: Method of moments applied to quasi-static antennas in media with dielectric anisotropy: Convergence study
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: It is studied how the method of moments can be used for analysis of the quasi-static antennas in media with dielectric anisotropy. The main attention is focused on the case when the transverse and longitudinal components of the dielectric tensor have opposite signs so the refractive index surface is non-closed, i.e., there exists a resonance cone and the corresponding Green's function has a singularity on it. It is shown that the method of moments can be used for calculations even in such a case.

articleTitle: Electronically tunable phase shifter with enhanced phase behaviour at Ku band
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We present the design of a microwave phase shifter at Ku band for active steerable array devices, with enhancement in its phase range. The device is based on a hybrid coupler with two of its ports loaded with reflective circuits. The reflective circuit provides the tunable nature to the device by means of electrically tunable varactors. This circuit includes impedance transformation to extend its phase variation range. The document includes the design of the shifter components, mainly focused on the reflective circuit design, and a complete shifter design.

articleTitle: Considerations on series inductance and inductively coupled loop matching circuits for UHF RFID tags
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper reports a comparison between shunt-series inductance (SSI) and inductively coupled loop (ICL) matching circuits for Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Radio Frequency IDentification (RFID) tags. It is shown analytically that an optimized ICL circuit is fully equivalent to an optimized SSI circuit provided that some adjustments are made on the dipole antenna geometry. Numerical and experimental characterizations of the RFID tags built with both topologies confirm this equivalence.

articleTitle: A new quad-band diversity antenna with high isolation
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A new high isolation antenna array for multiband applications is presented. The proposed antenna consists of annular-ring slots printed on FR4 substrate and operates in quad bands for different applications such as DCS/higher GSM/LTE2500/WiMAX/HiperLAN bands. The isolation is achieved through a combination of hybrid isolation enhancement mechanisms. Firstly; the antennas are placed in an orthogonal arrangement to perform the required polarisation diversity. Then; a very thin Defected Wall Structure is being inserted between antennas to suppress the direct coupling. Moreover; additional strips are added to increases isolation. The proposed antenna is being investigated and verified both numerically and experimentally. The measurement and simulation results are in good agreement; the proposed antenna has been compared with previous works. However; the proposed antenna has some outstanding characteristics such as a geometric simplicity, compact size and low correlation which gives the antenna an excellent diversity performance and a good candidate for multiband applications.

articleTitle: An online supervised calibration scheme for time-varying MIMO channel measurement
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A calibration scheme for channel sounding techniques, known as the basis of wireless channel characterization, is especially presented for time-varying Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) channel measurement. This scheme is proposed to replace the conventional time-division switching method which is time consuming thus not suitable for the time-varying MIMO channel measurement. Our proposed online supervised calibration scheme simultaneously considers multiple transmitting and receiving antenna pairs as a multi-channel time-varying complex system, and can take care of not only combined channel responses of all transmitting and receiving antenna pairs, but also baseband jitters in each pair during the measurement. Verification measurement shows the differences of RF channel responses are perfectly compensated using calibration data at the post-processing stage. Specifically, the variance of the delay across 8∗8 parallel MIMO channel is reduced from 3.028 ns to 0.048 ns since the calibration scheme is implemented.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Half-mode substrate-integrated cavity antenna arrays
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A frequency-reconfigurable array of HMSIW cavity antennas is presented in this paper. The tuning of the frequency is controlled using stub-loaded varactors. The feeding network can be designed so that the antenna either operates with omni-directional or broadside patterns. Two antenna arrays have been designed demonstrating a frequency tuning range of about 27% from 3.05 GHz to 4.0 GHz. The overall simulated efficiency, including the feeding network, is better than 56% for the omni-directional antenna and 42% for the broadside antenna.

articleTitle: A supersonic projectile — embedded OFDM channel sounder. First validation experimental results
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A new concept of embeddable channel sounder based on the OFDM modulation scheme is proposed. A first prototype has been has been designed, embedded into a supersonic projectile and tested in real conditions. These measurements have enabled us to validate the technique with the determination of the path loss and small scale effect behavior of a supersonic speed wireless channel.

articleTitle: A cost-effective set-up for time modulated array measurement using software defined radio
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper a new measurement technique suitable for Time Modulated Array antennas is proposed, which utilizes a low-cost, small form factor, versatile Software Defined Radio (SDR). Performance of the SDR is compared to a spectrum analyzer and the difference is extracted for further calibration. Radiation pattern of a TMA with a defined switching sequence is measured by the SDR, and compared to the simulated array factor. The measured and simulation results are in good agreement, which confirms the accuracy and reliability of the proposed measurement technique.

articleTitle: Compact UWB circularly polarized dielectric rod antenna design
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel circular-polarization (CP) ultrawideband dielectric rod antenna design has been developed for operating from X to Ka band. The radiation tip design was based on the previous dual linear-polarization 3-layer dielectric rod design. A novel CP wave-launcher composed of conical spiral arms was developed. This launcher does not require balun or quadrature-phase hybrid. In addition, a novel quadrifilar conducting enclosure was introduced to minimize overall antenna diameter while maintaining good axial ratio at the low frequency end. The simulated antenna performance exhibits an axial ratio (AR) of less than 3 dB, stable gain, stable beamwidth, and stable phase center from 10 to 40 GHz.

articleTitle: A low-profile 2D tilted-beam resonant cavity antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A low-profile tilted-beam resonant cavity antenna (RCA) based on gradient artificial magnetic conductor (AMC) and partially reflective surface (PRS) is proposed in this paper. The AMC is composed of an array of square patch printed on a dielectric substrate with metal ground backed, while the PRS consists of complementary arrays of square loop patch and aperture, which are printed on both sides of a dielectric slab. The reflection phase gradient of PRS and AMC can be controlled separately by gradating the sizes of their unit cells along orthogonal directions, leading to the capability of RCA to achieve beam-tilting in 2D domain. An implementation is demonstrated with simulated results, which manifests the feasibility of the design method.

articleTitle: New wideband wearable notch antennas for energy harvesting applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Wide band efficient wearable antennas are crucial for energy harvesting wearable systems. Notch and Slot antennas are low profile and low cost and may be employed in energy harvesting wearable systems. The efficiency of energy harvesting wearable systems may be improved by using active wearable notch and slot antennas. Small printed antennas suffer from low efficiency. Amplifiers may be connected to the wearable antenna feed line to increase the system dynamic range. Novel active wearable antennas for energy harvesting applications are presented in this paper. The notch antennas bandwidth is from 50% to 100% with VSWR better than 3:1. The notch antenna gain is around 3dBi with efficiency higher than 90%. The antennas electrical parameters was computed in vicinity of the human body. The active antenna gain is 24±2.5dB for frequencies ranging from 200MHz to 900MHz. The active antenna gain is 12.5±2.5dB for frequencies ranging from 1GHz to 3GHz. The active notch antenna Noise Figure is 0.5±0.3dB for frequencies ranging from 200MHz to 3.3GHz.

articleTitle: The design of high-responsivity millimeter wave imager using vanadium dioxide microbolometers
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A new class of millimeter wave (mmW) imaging sensor using a phase-change material (PCM) microbolometer is designed and presented. In this approach, non-linear and large change in electrical resistivity of antenna-coupled vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) bolometer are exploited to achieve high responsivity, fast response time, and low noise equivalent power (NEP). The sensor is biased near the phase transition cliff temperature of 68 °C. Micro-electro-mechanical Systems (MEMS) microfabrication process is utilized to suspend the sensor in air to improve the thermal resistance and therefore overall performance of the sensor. Preliminary simulation results, together with analytical studies, demonstrate approximately 30 times improvement in responsivity (9.4×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> V/W) and 60% reduction in NEP (5.5 pW/VHz) as compared to the state-of-the-art sensor. The corresponding rise time and fall time of the device are 6 °C and 35 μs, respectively. In the near future, a pixilated array of the proposed sensor enables the realization of highly sensitive mmW camera for variety of sensing applications.

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of nonuniform helical antennas for detection of side-channel attacks in computer systems
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a design, fabrication and measurement results of a helical antenna that has variable pitch angle and radius. These variations allow the nonuniform helix to be for 2–3 dB more directive compared to the optimal uniform helix of the same length (750 mm). A 3D printed support structure for the helix to be wound around is made out of ABS plastic and a 400 mm by 400 mm metal sheet is used as the ground plane. The design frequency is 2 GHz, the impedance bandwidth is 33% (1.8 GHz-2.5 GHz), and the axial ratio is less than 3.8 dB. The gain is 18.2 dBi and the two prototypes that are built match the simulation performance<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>.

articleTitle: Design guidelines for printable magnetic shielding films for NFC tags on metal
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The performance of RFID tags deteriorates when mounted on metallic objects. This is due to the induced eddy current effect on the metal which produces a magnetic field that opposes the reader/ tag field. Suitable electromagnetic screening is needed to mitigate this issue e.g. ferromagnetic films shielding the tag from the metal. This paper explores some design guidelines for ferrite films properties for additive manufacturing methods. Simulated and measured results for different ferromagnetic films and their influence on the performance of the NFC tags are investigated.

articleTitle: An accurate closed-form design for microstrip directional couplers with compensative capacitances
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a closed-form, analytical design of microstrip coupler with high directivity using compensative capacitances. The paper first proposes a new concept of quasi homogenous medium for compensated microstrip coupling lines. The design method utilizes quasi-static analysis and conformal mapping technique to develop the first set of equations for distribution capacitances necessary to calculate compensative capacitances. The approach also adopts symmetry analysis and equivalency principals to derive the second set of equations to calculate compensative capacitance and find out the factors of broadband response. The agreement of two groups of compensated values verifies the accuracy of two sets of equations. To validate the presented concept, equations and closed-form design method, two −20dB couplers with different bandwidths were completed with the available numerical values, simulation and measurement results. All results confirm the accuracy of the presented design method.

articleTitle: An efficient domain cascading approach for linear discontinuous Galerkin schemes
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A discontinuous Galerkin finite element method based domain decomposition technique is presented for solving Maxwell's Equations. The method can be implemented with either time domain or frequency domain solutions for sub-domains. The problem in each sub domain is solved using open boundaries. A connection in frequency domain is then established between the solved outward and inward fluxes of the sub-domains touching each other. No field continuity is imposed giving the technique high computational efficiency due to the lack of Schwarz iterations. The sub-domains are cascaded in a non-iterative manner. The methods' core elements are verified by comparing them to commercial solvers using a two-element antenna problem and a periodic boundary problem in 2D space.

articleTitle: Convex lenses horn antenna microwave hyperthermia scheme
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a new preclinical microwave hyperthermia system based on the combination among horn antenna and convex lenses. The horn antenna is designed to resonate at 3 GHz which is reported for hyperthermia therapy. Two convex lenses are designed and incorporated with the designed horn antenna and the reported breast phantom. The proposed system aims to heat up the tumor region above 42<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup>C while keeping the surrounding area temperature unchanged as possible to protect them from damage. Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) and breast phantom thermal distribution are studied with and without using lenses at different inclination angles. The proposed system has the advantage of heating up different zones separately while keeping other regions temperature unchanged. Simulation results show that, the breast temperature can be elevated by 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">°</sup> C above the normal body temperature.

articleTitle: Ku-band grounded dielectric slab based asymmetric Bull's-eye antenna fed by monopole
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this work, a Bull's-Eye (BE) leaky wave antenna (LWA) consisting of two sets of five semicircular copper strips over a grounded dielectric slab, asymmetrically distributed around a central radiating monopole is presented. The antenna operates at 13 GHz and shows a gain of 19.4 dBi with a side lobe level of −17.3 dB (−20.3 dB for the numerical ideal case at f = 12.6 GHz) and a narrow 6° beam. It presents lower side lobe levels than a radiating slot metallic BE-LWA due to the null radiation of the monopole in the direction normal to the surface and maximum radiation in the transversal direction.

articleTitle: A single antenna radar sensor with FMCW radar transceiver IC
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a single antenna radar sensor with Ku-band radar transceiver IC realized in 0.13 μm CMOS processes. In the radar receiver, a sensitivity time control using a DC offset cancellation feedback loop is employed for constant SNR irrelevant on the distance. To reduce the direct coupled Tx signal to Rx in single antenna radar, stub tuned hybrid coupler is adopted instead of circulator. The measured distance is 8.2 m with horn antenna and metal plate target.

articleTitle: Optimal synthesis of wideband planar phased arrays with maximum bandwidth
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The synthesis of wideband planar arrays with fixed elements position and arbitrary upper power bounds on the side-lobes of the far field pattern is addressed in this work. An optimal strategy based on a convex programming (CP) procedure is proposed to define the set of excitations satisfying the power constraints, jointly maximizing the antenna operating bandwidth. Preliminary numerical results are given and discussed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Ku-band RF aperture assembly for airborne SOTM
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the design basis, development and main results for a KU-Band RF Aperture Assembly for Airborne SOTM (SatCom on the Move) comprising the main aspects: the antenna panel, low noise amplification and both Rx and Tx structures for polarisation Skew. The aperture consists of a flat wideband antenna panel, diplexer, low noise amplifiers and independent polarization control to receive and transmit Ku-band. The block provides full duplex receiving and transmission functionality and all the requirements for aeroplane operation when integrated into a SOTM whole system. The block exhibits key characteristics, a high integration level and performance.

articleTitle: High sensitivity inkjet-printed terahertz metallic hole array sensor
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Surface plasmon resonance sensors based on the resonant transmission characteristics of metal hole arrays are fabricated using conductive inkjet printing for operation in the terahertz region. The response of the sensing surfaces is measured using terahertz time domain spectroscopy. The addition of a layer of glycerol on the surface that is much thinner than the wavelength of the incident wave is simulated and results in a significant shift of the resonance frequency. This indicates the possibility of realising a flexible low-cost sensor for chemical and biological substances.

articleTitle: Polarization control of bulk acoustic wave-mediated multiferroic antennas based on thickness shear modes
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel electrically-small bulk acoustic wave (BAW)-mediated multiferroic antenna is proposed based on transverse shear waves instead of the longitudinal ones used in the previously proposed multiferroic antenna [1]. Two in-plane orthogonal pairs of electrodes provide independent excitation of the orthogonal transverse shear modes, enabling the first investigation of polarization control in a BAW-mediated multiferroic antenna. Using this approach, polarization can be controlled simply by adjusting the phase difference between the input RF signals of the two electrode pairs. The proposed design concept is verified numerically via COMSOL simulations and a series of post-processing steps in MATLAB. By assuming ideal input RF signals with equal amplitude and 90° phase difference, broadband circularly polarized radiation is achieved in the sub-GHz band.

articleTitle: Broadband superluminal transmission line with non-foster negative capacitor
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: We present a superluminal transmission line (STL) loaded with non-Foster negative capacitors. The loaded negative capacitors decrease the effective capacitance and the effective permittivity of the dielectric substrate of the TL. Since wave propagation velocity depends on effective capacitance of the line, it can be higher than the light speed c<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> in vacuum. The superluminal line is simulated and the results are compared to an experimental investigation of the superluminal phase and group velocities that are extracted from measured S-parameters.

articleTitle: A rain model for the tropics based on TRMM data fitted to DBSG3
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Distributions of point one-minute rain rates are fundamental for modelling rain attenuation on terrestrial and earth-space communication links. The current Recommendation of the International Telecommunication Union — Radiocommunication Sector, ITU-R P.837-6 provides these distributions globally, derived from Numerical Weather Products, but is widely considered inaccurate in the tropics. This paper presents a rain distribution model for the tropics derived from Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission satellite data. Downscaling from TRMM distributions to one-minute distributions is performed by fitting to a subset of data within the database of the ITU-R Study Group 3, DBSG3. The results are verified against the remaining DBSG3 data using the Rec ITU-R P.311 Goodness of Fit measure.

articleTitle: A linear perturbation model with physical optics approximation to recover inhomogeneous surface impedance
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Inverse electromagnetic scattering problems related to objects having inhomogeneous isotropic impedance boundaries are addressed by considering small impedance variations between a measured object and a reference one. For many non-destructive electromagnetic testing, the structure geometries are known and only coated materials properties variations from reference numerical model are of interest. Consequently, the scattered field and equivalent surface current of the reference object can be precisely evaluated. We use the Chu-Stratton integral equation to express the differences of scattered far field between the measured and reference configurations in terms of surface current variation. Physical Optics approximation is used to derive a model of these surface current variations and we keep the first order term to solve a linear inverse problem. Consequently, the surface impedance can be reconstructed by a minimum norm solution in the least squares sense. Some promising numerical results on spherical geometries are presented with fixed incidence and frequency, in bistatic configuration.

articleTitle: Inter-link interference measurement of indoor dense millimeter-wave WLANs
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: An exponential increase in the number of smart mobile devices with high demands of wireless data traffic is driving Wireless Local Area Networks (WLANs) toward high-density deployments and millimeter-wave (mmWave) operations. Inter-link interference is a crucial factor in such systems, which impacts on the link performance and system capacity. However, it has not been well-investigated yet. We conducted a measurement campaign on inter-link interference in a meeting room environment with dense deployment of mmWave WLANs. Some key impact factors, such as the beamwidths and positions of transmitter and receiver as well as the number of active links in a network, were investigated. Our measurement results demonstrate that the decrease of the beamwidths of transmitter and receiver and/or the decrease of the number of active links in the network can significantly improve the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) due to reduction of the inter-link interference. Furthermore, it is observed that the inter-link interference in a dense deployment environment mainly depends on a few dominated active links.

articleTitle: Advanced physical phantoms for evaluation of medical antennas and devices
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Recently, wireless medical antennas and devices have been widely used. It is almost impossible to use a real human body to evaluate in-body medical antennas and devices experimentally. Instead, human-body physical phantoms are inevitable for such experiments. This paper firstly overviews a few points of human-body physical phantoms. Then, two typical examples of advanced physical phantoms, namely, an inhomogeneous phantom and a transparent phantom are briefly introduced as semi-hard phantoms.

articleTitle: Time of flight sphere-based reconstruction algorithm and processing techniques for multi-monostatic portal-based scanners
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A set of algorithms fits a surface to a point cloud that is produced by a time of flight sphere based reconstruction algorithm for multi-monostatic millimeter-wave security scanners. Simulated results suggest that the ultra-fast algorithm is effective at fitting smooth surfaces to point clouds containing spurious points, enabling easier interpretation of the reconstructed image of the target.

articleTitle: Slotted substrate integrated waveguide antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A novel Slotted Substrate integrated waveguide (SSIW) antenna is presented at 2.5 GHz. Computer simulation technology (CST) has been used to design the antenna and the effect of design parameters are demonstrated. The comparison between measurement and simulation results are also presented and shown to be in good agreement. The return loss for the measurements was below 15dB and the gain at 2.5 GHz is 16.2 dBi.

articleTitle: Analysis of rain rate estimations in tropical regions using a 5 GHz microwave link
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The estimation of rain rate using microwave links has been explored in the past mainly in temperate climates and for frequencies above 5 GHz. This investigation analyses the effectiveness of a variation of the ITU-R P.838 recommendation to estimate rain rate using a 5 GHz radio link in the tropical city of Guayaquil. The measured attenuation due to rainfall over the link was too low to be considered of any practical use, however unexpectedly large values of attenuation were measured when rain was observed at the transmitter site. It was discovered that the cause of this relatively high level of attenuation was the wetting of the antenna; this phenomenon was accurately modeled by a power relationship similar to the one used to estimate attenuation caused by rainfall over a radio link.

articleTitle: Discrete page spectrum in analzying phenomena in linear antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper deals with Discrete Page Transformation (DPT). With DPT a transient response of antenna with resistive inclusions was investigated. Antenna was excited with Gaussian pulse voltage. DPT transforms signal from the time domain into two dimensional time-frequency domain. The examples shows that with Discrete Page Spectrum (DPS) it is easy to separate the reflected signal energy from heterogeneity of antenna. What is more, DPT allows to separate energy associated with individual antenna resonances.

articleTitle: Wideband millimeter-wave end-fire magneto-electric dipole antenna fed by substrate integrated coaxial line
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A wideband millimeter-wave magneto-electric (ME) dipole antenna with end-fire radiation, which is fed by the substrate integrated coaxial line (SICL), is designed, fabricated, and measured. First, the ME-dipole antenna excited by a planar L-probe is presented to realize wideband performance. Then, a wideband impedance conversion structure is used to connect the antenna and the feeding port. A simple conversion structure for the SICL to the grounded coplanar waveguide is used for the antenna test. Finally, the simulation and measurement results validate the proposed end-fire ME-dipole antenna. The overall bandwidth is greater than 40% considering both impedance bandwidth and 3-dB gain bandwidth.

articleTitle: Characteristic of spatial distributed field on marine environment with multi-ships and wakes
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The spatial distributed scattering field information is of great importance to the recognition and detection of ship targets in marine environment for the highresolution radar system. For this goal, the sea surface and the interested targets are divided into small patches, which establishes the foundation of geometry. Then the combination of the capillary wave modification facet scattering model (CWMFSM) and the geometrical optics and physical optics method (GO-PO) method is employed for the analyses of spatial distributed scattering field on such a marine environment containing ships and the generated wakes. The analyses provide a new perspective to detect and recognize complex ship targets on sea surface in modern high-resolution radar system. The results show that the influence of the coupling scattering is essential. Besides, some structures are shown as strong scattering sources in the spatial distributed image, which can be exploited to help the recognition of target structures in SAR images.

articleTitle: A wideband base station antenna with reduced beam squint
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents the design procedure, theoretical analysis, and experimental results of a novel wideband dual-polarized base station antenna. The proposed antenna consists of four electric folded dipoles arranged in an octagon shape that are excited simultaneously for each polarization. It provides the ±45° slant-polarized radiation that meets all the required specifications for base station antenna elements.
