Experimental results show that the proposed dual-polarized antenna has a wide bandwidth of 46.4% from 1.69 GHz to 2.71 GHz with ≥ 15 dB return loss. Across this wide bandwidth, the variations of the half-power-beamwidths (HPBWs) of the two polarizations are all within 66.5° ± 5.5°, port-to-port isolation is > 30 dB, the cross-polarization discrimination (XPD) is > 20 dB and, most importantly, the beam squint is < 4° with a maximum 10° down-tilt.

articleTitle: Mechanical beam steering circular patch antenna
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This work reports preliminary results and a prototype of an innovative mechanical beam steering circular patch antenna for 5G indoor cellular access networks with sub-6 GHz operation. The beam steering is achieved using 18 screws installed around the circular patch radiator, working as a reflector by proper managing the screws position and height. The new antenna can steer its main beam over 360° in azimuth plane and from −30° to 30° in the elevation plane with gain up to 8.01 dBi at 4.6 GHz.

articleTitle: Compressive sensing for inverse problems
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This work is devoted to the presentation of the recent advances of Compressive Sensing (CS) as applied to inverse scattering problems. A review of the theoretical fundamentals of CS and of the state-of-the-art methodologies is presented. Moreover, the main issues concerning inverse scattering problems are discussed in order to comply with the CS paradigm assumptions. Two representative numerical results, considering both bi-dimensional and tri-dimensional problems, are reported showing the effectiveness of CS based techniques.

articleTitle: Radar Doppler technique to estimate the energy expenditure of human physical activities
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The estimation of activity-related energy expenditure during a day is an important parameter to be calculated and monitored, especially in Ambient Assisted Living application for elders. In fact, scientific evidences exist that a sedentary life has serious physiological and heart implications. Many are the compact and wearable measuring devices currently available, such as pedometers and accelerometers. Anyway, in the view of Ambient Assisted Living application, contactless and no-collaborative systems are to be preferred. For this reason, in this paper an alternative approach for activity-related energy expenditure calculation based on an electromagnetic contactless motion sensor is proposed. The velocity and kinetic energy associated to a moving target are calculated from the elaboration of spectrogram intensity. The method has been firstly validated with a well-known movement, i.e. the swinging of a physical pendulum, and then tested with a human subject moving his arm, with very promising results.

articleTitle: Miniaturized spoof surface plasmon polaritons transmission line
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Based on via arrays, a novel miniaturized spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) transmission line (TL) with enhanced slow wave effect is proposed in this paper. The proposed miniaturized SSPPs TL is a bilateral metal structure connected by via arrays, composed of a pair of low impedance slotlines, a pair of flaring transitions and a section of corrugated metal strip. Excited by low impedance slotline, the bilateral structure transmits SSPPs from 2 GHz to 10 GHz and obtains a strong slow wave effect. In this paper, the designed structure and sample fabrication are presented. Simulated and measured S-parameters match well. High transmission efficiency and the enhanced slow wave effect are obtained. Moreover, the proposed structure halves the size compared to conventional planar SSPPs TLs excited by coplanar waveguide. These features give important potentials to develop integrated SSPPs devices and slow wave circuits.

articleTitle: High-frequency characterization of EMI/EMC ground test facility for the measurements of electric propulsion thruster emissions
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper an electromagnetic characterization of an EMI/EMC test facility for electric propulsion thrusters is presented. The facility consists of a dielectric vacuum chamber placed in a semi-anechoic room and connected to a Large Vacuum Test Facility. To this end, an analysis of the electromagnetic field radiated outside a canonical infinite dielectric cylinder by an internal line source has been conducted. First the two-dimensional Green's Function for the electromagnetic radiation by a line source inside the canonical dielectric hollow cylinder is developed. Then, two high frequency emission models based on Geometrical Optics and on an iterative implementation of the Physical Optics are formulated and the results compared to those of the Green's function method. The numerical results show very good agreement between the simplified high frequency techniques and the exact formulation.

articleTitle: Equivalent circuit model for cross-shaped frequency selective surface absorbing material
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The equivalent circuit model is used to analyze the actual structure of the multilayer frequency selective surface absorbing. The transmission line model and equivalent impedance are provided for the transmissivity of electromagnetic waves. The results are validated by comparison with the Ansoft HFSS. In addition, the influences of different parameters are discussed. It is found that such a multilayer absorbing material has a good tenability and independence for the absorption frequency. This can be used to design absorbing material for different requirements.

articleTitle: Compound reflection metagrating for wideband backscattering reduction
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, we experimentally demonstrate a wideband backscattering reduction in the terahertz (THz) range by using a metallic compound reflection metagrating (CRMG). A strong and broadband backscattering reduction (with fractional bandwidth, FBW ≈ 57%) is achieved by efficiently transferring the incident energy to the diffracted modes. The measurements are in perfect agreement with results obtained using an analytical equivalent circuit and numerical simulations. The presented design can find applications in radar and telecommunication systems.

articleTitle: Circularly polarized electrically small antennas for emerging wireless applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper introduces three circularly-polarized (CP) electrically small antennas for emerging wireless applications including wireless power transfer (WPT), Internet-of-Things (IoT), and Device-to-Device (D2D) communications in future fifth generation (5G) systems. First, an electrically small Huygens CP (HCP) antenna operating at L-band frequencies is presented that is facilitated by two near-field resonant parasitic (NFRP) elements, a crossed Egyptian axe dipole (EAD) pair and a crossed capacitively loaded loop (CLL) pair. The HCP antenna is electrically small (ka = 0.73), low profile (∼ 0.04λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), and has decent cardioid-shaped radiation patterns with a broad half power beamwidth (>120°). It is attractive for many WPT and body-centric wireless sensor network applications. Second, with the rapid development of 5G wireless networks, a corresponding 28 GHz electrically small HCP antenna is reported. The overall size of this antenna is only π (1.5)<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> × 1 ≈ 7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (ka = 0.94), which can be readily integrated into the various compact platforms anticipated for 5G IoT devices. Third, unlike the above two antennas that radiate uni-directional patterns, a compact 28 GHz omni-directional CP (OCP) antenna is presented for D2D communications in future 5G systems. It is electrically small (ka = 0.95), easy to fabricate, and its performance characteristics cover the entire FCC-specified 5G, 27.5 to 28.35 GHz band.

articleTitle: Long-term spectrum monitoring and occupancy from 174 to 1000 MHz in rural western Montana
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Fixed and mobile spectrum monitoring stations were implemented to study the spectrum range from 174 to 1000 MHz in rural locations within the mountains of western Montana, USA. This work identifies available channels of 5 MHz or larger bandwidth as candidates for a remote mobile broadband network. The long-term measurements show that the majority of channels in this spectrum range are not detectably utilized and are candidates for spectrum sharing.

articleTitle: Measurements of UWB pulse propagation along a wind turbine blade at 1 to 20 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper describes propagation measurements of an Ultra Wide Band (UWB) pulse along a full-scale wind turbine blade. The aim is to use the UWB channel characteristics to determine the deflection of the wind turbine blade under different wind loads. The frequency response is measured from 1 to 20 GHz and by use of Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) studied the delay domain. It has been found challenging to determine the deflection of the blade only by looking at the delay difference between the Line-Of-Sight (LOS) pulse and a pulse reflected from the blade. To determine from which area of the blade the reflection originates a ray-tracing study incorporating a model of the curvature of the blade have been conducted. This showed the area causing the reflections depended highly on the placement of the antenna on the wind turbine blade.

articleTitle: Robust design of low side lobe level microstrip antenna array by using lossy superstrate
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The side lobe level (SLL) suppression technique using lossy superstrate for robust antenna design is proposed. It is conduct by optimizing the dielectric parameters (i.e., relative permittivity, thickness and loss tangent) based on the spectral Green's function. To validate our method, a 2∗2 microstrip antenna array loaded by 2-layer dielectric superstrate is optimized for low SLL. The optimization results show that using lossless dielectric superstrate the optimized SLL can reach −35.2 dB at 35 GHz without considering the fabrication error. Taking the available precision of air gap thickness (±0.02 mm) into consideration, the SLL is raised to −30.4 dB while using lossy superstrate it can be reduced to −35.6 dB at the cost of gain by 5.6 dB. With involving the effect of the feed network in the simulation, the SLL is deteriorated to −34 dB and is lower than −32.3 dB over the operating band from 34.65 GHz to 35.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Research advances in phased array antennas for satellite communications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Recent research advances in phased array antennas for mobile satellite communications in the State Key Laboratory of Millimeter Waves (SKLMMW) are reviewed, including the Ku-band multiple-panel phased array antenna with almost half sphere coverage, the Ka-band low cost linear phased array module for planar array applications, a single board dual polarized S-band phased array for China S-band mobile satellite communications. The development for fast phased array calibration and measurement is also introduced.

articleTitle: Design of multiband circularly polarized antenna arrays for GNSS applications
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Two Multiband circularly polarized antenna arrays are proposed in this paper. Both of the antenna arrays consist of four antenna elements. Each antenna element has three patches, generating circular polarization electromagnetic wave at three frequency bands. The antenna arrays can operate at GPS L1, L2, and L5 bands. The slits are used in the second antenna array to achieve lower mutual coupling between the antenna elements compared with the first antenna array. Simulations and measurements are carried out to study the antenna element and antenna arrays' performances in terms of impedance matching, axial ratio, gain and radiation patterns. Both of simulation and measurement results are shown to illustrate the good performance of the proposed antenna arrays. It is very suitable for multi-functional GNSS applications.

articleTitle: Wideband low-profile transmitarray antenna for backhauling at 60 GHz
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: A low profile transmitarray architecture composed of four profiled focal sources and a flat-lens array is discussed in this paper. The flat-lens is a square array with 2116 unit-cells disposed on a 46x46 element regular grid. Considering the proposed focal system, the focal distance is equal to 44.6 mm (F/D ratio equal to 0.39), which must be compared to a F/D ratio equal to 0.7 corresponding to the case of a transmitarray with classical focal sources with a gain of 10 - 12 dBI. The flat-lens array is based on seven unit-cells with a relative phase-shift around 45° and a transmission coefficient high than -1.9dB in the frequency band 57-66 GHZ (14.6% at 61.5 GHz). The full-arry has been optimized using an ad-hoc tool and results compared to full-wave simulations. A maximum gain of 36 dBi has been obtained including the impact of the waveguide power divider. The 1-dB and 3-dB gain bandwidth are equal to12.4% and 23.2%, respectively.

articleTitle: Towards an experimental validation of microwave imaging monitoring of thermal ablation treatments
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This communication describes the ongoing efforts towards the assessment of microwave imaging as a tool for real-time monitoring of thermal ablation treatments. In particular, the ex-vivo experimental set-up adopted for the validation is described, and the results of a preliminary experiment are shown. Notably, by analyzing pre- and postablation treatment data it is possible to recognize the footprint of the interface between the ablated and not-ablated tissue, making it possible to estimate the boundary of the treated area.

articleTitle: Accurate scattering matrix reconstruction for multi-element antennas — application to hybrid arrays
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The design of multi-element antennas, including especially phased arrays and parasitic element arrays, requires synthesis methods to determine the weights to be addressed on each radiating element in order to satisfy a set of specifications on the radiated pattern. To be reliable and realistic, this synthesis must be accurate to take into account the coupling parameters between the radiating elements. To avoid the prohibitive CPU time linked to full-wave approaches, a formalism derived from periodic boundaries is proposed. The main novelty is to get the full scattering matrix in a general case, contrary to classical formalism where only the active reflection coefficient is determined. This approach is then integrated into a synthesis approach and applied to the synthesis of an original array. This one allows the optimization of the effective area of the panel with only a few number of active channels.

articleTitle: Cellular networks backhauling through satellite: Performance evaluation using alphasat site diversity experiment in Greece
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, propagation data from ALPHASAT Ka Band site diversity experiment in Greece are utilized in order to evaluate a cellular networks satellite backhauling scenario. An emulator is developed taking as input cellular networks capacity requirements and the real-time propagation time series (atmospheric attenuation) from both satellite ground terminals. Afterwards, exploiting the site diversity setup, a simple heuristic capacity allocation scheme is proposed for the minimization of the capacity losses. Some interesting conclusions are drawn.

articleTitle: Retrieving the constitutive parameters of metal-backed radar absorbing material by phase unwrapping method
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, we present a phase unwrapping method to unambiguously retrieve the constitutive parameters of metal-backed radar absorbing material (RAM) over the frequency range of 2–18 GHz from the reflection coefficients of slabs with two different thicknesses. Compared with the traditional transmission and reflection method, for example, Nicolson-Ross-Weir (NRW) algorithm, the presented method depends on properly compensating propagation factor with different phase values over specific frequency ranges to resolve the phase ambiguity during the retrieving process. The method is demonstrated over metal-backed magnetic RAM and the validity is confirmed by the good agreement between the retrieved results and the existing experimental data over 2–18 GHz frequency range.

articleTitle: Wireless power transfer: Exposure assessment for grounded and ungrounded human body
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This study compares the exposure of a grounded and ungrounded human body to a representative resonant wireless power transfer (WPT) system. A Duke human body model is adopted all along the paper. Exposure levels with respect to the ICNIRP basic restrictions are assessed as a function of the distance between the WPT system and the ground, and reported in terms of dosimetric quantities E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">99</inf>, J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1cm2</inf>, as well as local and whole body SAR. Maximum allowable input power is computed for the considered scenarios. The results demonstrate that, peak dosimetric values are much higher in grounded than ungrounded scenarios independently of the distance of the WPT system from the ground. For the grounded cases, as the WPT system gets closer to the ground, higher exposure levels are induced inside the body in terms of J<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1cm2</inf> and SAR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10g</inf> as a difference to E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">99</inf> and SAR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">wb</inf>. Moreover, SAR<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10g</inf> is found to be the most restrictive dosimetric quantity.

articleTitle: Agile method for antenna polarization characterization based on amplitude measurements
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The improvement of the accuracy of the polarimetrie parameters provided by weather radars depends on the accurate knowledge of the polarization pattern of the radar antenna. Most polarization measurement methods rely on the assumption of ideal probes. In this paper, a method for polarization measurement that does not require ideal probes is presented. The method is completely based on voltage amplitude measurements.

articleTitle: The generation of circular polarization in cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna using an arc-shaped dielectric element
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a technique Is proposed to achieve the circularly polarized radiations in the dielectric resonator (DR) antenna. An arc-shaped DR element is applied at the periphery of the half cylindrical DR to obtain the circular polarization. The 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 13.56% ranging from 3.23–3.70 GHz. The antenna provides the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth of 5.84% in the frequency range 3.49–3.70 GHz. The antenna can be utilized in the 3.3–3.8 GHz WiMAX applications.

articleTitle: On the improvement of the power transfer efficiency between radiating apertures
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The power transfer efficiency in Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) systems depends on the field distribution supported by the transmitter and the receiver. A network analysis is here developed to characterize the effect of the field distribution supported by the transmitter and the receiver over the power efficiency of the system. Numerical results show that a Bessel-Gaussian-like distribution exhibits better power transfer efficiency with respect to the other considered field distribution. Such phenomenon is attributed to the non-diffractive nature of the radiated energy.

articleTitle: Polarization scattering matrix estimation for uniform moving target
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, we deal with the problem of polarization scattering matrix (PSM) estimation for moving targets in the presence of Gaussian clutter. To this end, we first formulate the measurement model for time-sharing polarimetric radar, and then jointly examine the influence of radar wavelength and target states on the scattering matrix estimation. For estimation purposes, we assume that a set of observation data is available with the same scattering matrix. As the performance of pulse integration declines when the target is in motion, we derive a novel method of phase compensation to estimate the moving target scattering matrix. Compared with pulse integration, the proposed method shows excellent performance, and numerical results validate the proposed method.

articleTitle: Impact of source antenna beamwidth on antenna measurement accuracy at DSRC frequencies
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: Multiple working groups are developing antenna performance requirements for V2x or dedicated short range communication systems to ensure the safety and reliability of this system. The preliminary specifications call for antenna measurements to be conducted at elevation angle extending from six degrees below the antenna horizon to ten degrees above the horizon. Antenna measurements made below the horizon can be challenging for existing antenna ranges due to the architecture of its elevation gantry. This paper studies the impact of antenna measurement accuracy at an outdoor automotive antenna range for an omni-directional antenna and a directional antenna as a function of source antenna half-power beamwidth and antenna height. The results are important to the measurement procedures that will be utilized to validate the final antenna performance specifications.

articleTitle: Clutter analysis in a time-domain millimeter-wave reflectometry setup
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this work, we study the clutter and multi-path propagation in a time-domain millimeter-wave reflectometry setup, used for material characterization or short-range imaging. The signal energy and fidelity factor of the different reflection components is analyzed in dependence of the distance from the target. Due to the change in pulse distortion in the multi-path components, the system impulse response is dependent on the target position. The principal reflection from the target on the other hand is only influenced by the path loss. By coherent superposition we are able to separate the target reflection from the static system clutter and multi-path reflections in the setup.

articleTitle: Verifying the geometric accuracy of Sentinel-IA and Sentinel-IB using L0-products
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: The geometric accuracy of Sentinel-1 is usally derived from level-1 products in Stripmap mode using accurate surveyed corner reflector positions. While the range offset is found to be low (∼30 cm) an azimuth offset of about 2 m remains. The study investigates the reason for the geometric offsets by deriving the geometric parameters from L0-data. Therefore the pulse round-trip time is analyzed from transmission to reception of a point target's backscatter including a simple pulse compression in range and azimuth. Finally, the azimuth offset is reduced to about 15 cm which indicates an artificial bias arising from SAR processing.

articleTitle: Design of hook type dipole phased array with anti-metal structure for 5G mobile terminals
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: In this paper, a hook type dipole phased array with anti-metal structure for 5G mobile terminals is presented. The proposed antenna operates at 28GHz with a bandwidth of 2GHz and has a good beam-steering characteristic with more than 9.07dB gains and sidelobe level less 6.49dB in the scanning range of 0 to 60 degree. The proposed antenna occupied a volume of 42.4×10.3×0.508mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, which can be easily fit into current mobile devices for the coming 5G short range communication standards.

articleTitle: Spatially efficient chipless RFID tag, Screen-printed on flexible substrate
publicationTitle: 12th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP 2018)
abstract: This paper presents a novel Chipless RFID tag operating from 3 to 8 GHz. The developed tag has high coding density of 5.13 bits/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and is based on obtaining at least two bits from one resonator. The designed tag is screen-printed inhouse using manual screen printer using two different type of conductive ink. The investigation of the response of printed tag showed that substrate parameters and ink parameters are playing a vital role in affecting the RF performance of the printed tag. The substrate parameters can be un-modifiable for some application of Chipless RFID technology, so ink parameters are enhanced to obtain better RF performance for the printed version of Chipless RFID tag.
